item.title: Mavericks are actively exploring trade options, league …
item.description: Marc Stein: Busy weekend in Dallas. The Mavericks are actively exploring trade options, league sources say, while also preparing for Nos. 9 and 30 in Tuesday's draft and progressing toward in a conclusion in their coaching search.

item.title: Wolves looking to move up in the first round?
item.description: Philon’s workout is an indication the Wolves are canvassing their options in terms of moving up from No. 28 in the first round. The last time the Wolves moved up in the draft for a guard, they did so in a major way two years ago.

item.title: Wolves are set to play host to Alabama guard Labaron …
item.description: The Wolves are set to play host to Alabama guard Labaron Philon Jr. for an individual workout, a source told the Minnesota Star Tribune.

item.title: Boston has its eyes on Trey Murphy III and may try to …
item.description: Boston has its eyes on Trey Murphy III and may try to make a deal for the New Orleans two-way wing. The Celtics could throw a couple of first-round picks in a deal.

item.title: Portland reportedly would like to get in the Jaylen …
item.description: Portland reportedly would like to get in the Jaylen Brown sweepstakes if Boston makes him available. Except, right now, he’s not really available. Maybe in an Antetokounmpo trade (Boston would want that straight up), but don’t bet on Boston just shopping the All-NBA player coming off the best season of his career.

item.title: Wizards plan to draft AJ Dybantsa at No. 1?
item.description: The Washington Wizards currently plan to draft former BYU forward AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 overall pick, sources told Dallas Hoops Journal, with the franchise centered on him as the 2026 NBA Draft opens Tuesday.

item.title: I was told a short time ago the Celtics have …
item.description: Gery Woelfel: I was told a short time ago the Celtics have intensified their efforts to land Antetokounmpo. The source declined to get into the details. Another league source said he was told the Celtics were more receptive to moving star Jaylen Brown, although it’s unlikely he wound wind up in Milwaukee but rather with a third team. While the Celtics appear focused on landing Antetokounmpo, it is generally believed Miami remains the frontrunner for the two-time MVP.

item.title: Collin Gillespie’s four-year, $48 million deal to …
item.description: Jake Fischer: Collin Gillespie’s four-year, $48 million deal to return to Phoenix is fully guaranteed, sources say. Quite the well-deserved payday for the Villanova product after thriving for the Suns on a minimum salary last season.

item.title: By my projections Suns will be roughly $4.6M under the …
item.description: Keith Smith: By my projections Suns will be roughly $4.6M under the tax and $12.6M under the first apron after re-signing Collin Gillespie. Can create more room if they move on from Haywood Highsmith and/or Jamaree Bouyea. It'll get tight to avoid the first apron if they re-sign Mark Williams and Jordan Goodwin.

item.title: Collin Gillespie agrees to four-year, $48 million deal to return to Phoenix
item.description: Shams Charania: Free agent guard Collin Gillespie intends to sign a four-year, $48 million deal to return to the Phoenix Suns, sources tell ESPN. Gillespie spent three straight seasons on two-way contracts after going undrafted out of Villanova in 2022 and now earns a lucrative long-term deal.

item.title: Gillespie’s agents at Excel Sports Management, Jordan …
item.description: Shams Charania: Gillespie’s agents at Excel Sports Management, Jordan Gertler and James Dunleavy, negotiated a deal with Suns executives after teams became eligible to talk to their own free agents last weekend. The sides came together on a deal for a guard who has emerged as a significant member and success story of the team's new culture around grit and toughness. item.title: Isaiah Hartenstein expected to remain in OKC
item.description: Starting center Isaiah Hartenstein has a $28.5 million team option for the upcoming season. He’s expected to remain in Oklahoma City. The question among executives around the league is whether the Thunder will exercise their team option or decline it and work out a new multi-year deal at a lower average annual salary.

item.title: Lakers among teams monitoring Lu Dort’s availability
item.description: With Williams expected to return healthy next season, Mitchell, Cason Wallace, Jared McCain, and Alex Caruso in the fold, teams across the league are monitoring fellow starter Lu Dort’s availability. Dort has a team option for $17.22 million for the upcoming season that several front executives who spoke with HoopsHype are projecting the Thunder to exercise, then consider flipping Dort on the trade market. Should such a scenario happen, Dort has been linked with the Lakers and several other team

item.title: Dillon Brooks extension could be worth $25 million per season
item.description: In his first season with Phoenix, Brooks remained a strong defender, helped change the team’s culture, and became a 20-point-per-game scorer for the first time in his career. At 30, Brooks enters the upcoming season on the books for $21 million. Looking ahead, Brooks could earn a potential extension around an average of $25 million per season.

item.title: After being consistent role players for Oklahoma City …
item.description: After being consistent role players for Oklahoma City throughout the past season, league sources say opposing executives have circled the wagon on Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins. Both players saw limited action against the Spurs in the Conference Finals, despite being key contributors during the regular season, and would represent significant depth upgrades for most teams around the league.

item.title: Lastly, the Suns have also done some background on …
item.description: Lastly, the Suns have also done some background on Chicago Bulls guard Josh Giddey, HoopsHype has learned.

item.title: Brooklyn Nets have attempted to move up into the …
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have attempted to move up into the top-four range of the NBA Draft by dangling their No. 6 pick with future first-round draft picks, league sources told HoopsHype.

item.title: Bucks would consider retaining Jaylen Brown if they land him in Giannis Antetokounmpo deal
item.description: Despite some executives around the league assuming it would be a foregone conclusion that the Bucks would try to flip Brown to another team to get future first-round draft pick compensation as part of a rebuilding effort, it’s not a certainty. If the Celtics indeed acquire Antetokounmpo and Brown ends up going to the Bucks as part of the trade, the Bucks would consider keeping Brown, HoopsHype has learned.

item.title: The Clippers are also said to be interested in Brown …
item.description: The Clippers are also said to be interested in Brown and have future first-round draft picks available to dangle, including the fifth pick in the draft as a potential trade chip, along with a 2029 unprotected first-round draft pick from the Indiana Pacers from the Ivica Zubac trade, should they decide to pursue a trade.

item.title: Portland has discussed trying to acquire …
item.description: The Portland Trail Blazers have been involved in Antetokounmpo trade talks on multiple fronts. Portland has discussed trying to acquire Antetokounmpo, and as a potential facilitator because they have two future first-round Bucks swaps in 2028 and 2030, league sources said.

item.title: It’s worth noting that Nikola Jovic, Kasparas …
item.description: It’s worth noting that Nikola Jovic, Kasparas Jakucionis, and Pelle Larsson have each come up in different iterations of the Antetokounmpo trade talks, league sources told HoopsHype.

item.title: They are committed to bringing back their own free …
item.description: John Gambadoro: YES the Suns can afford both. They are committed to bringing back their own free agents and willing to go deep into the luxury tax to do that. They won't go into the second apron, but they shouldn't have to.

item.title: WE completed the mission together as brothers, and …
item.description: Kyrie Irving: All for one. One for All WE completed the mission together as brothers, and that’s all that matters to me. Hélà 🤞🏾♾🪶

item.title: After four seasons, I’ve left Sports Illustrated
item.description: Joey Linn: After four seasons, I’ve left Sports Illustrated. Starting now, and hopefully for a long time, I’ll be covering the LA Clippers independently. Thank you for the continued support. It’s made this possible. I hope you’ll join me at my new site.

item.title: Wolves have gauged trade value of Julius Randle, Donte DiVincenzo, and first-rounder
item.description: The Timberwolves have gauged the trade value of Julius Randle, Donte DiVincenzo, and their No. 28 first-round pick in the draft, league sources told HoopsHype.

item.title: Ayo Dosunmu projected to earn $18-20 million per season in free agency
item.description: After trading for Ayo Dosunmu at the deadline, the Minnesota Timberwolves want to re-sign him. According to NBA executives who’ve spoken with HoopsHype, Dosunmu’s range is projected to be somewhere north of $18 million annually and could reach the low $20 million range.

item.title: Other teams have always called on rising swingman …
item.description: Other teams have always called on rising swingman Jaden McDaniels. Minnesota has made him essentially untradable unless it was for a blockbuster trade involving Giannis Antetokounmpo or Nikola Jokic. When the Los Angeles Clippers were struggling earlier this season amid a 6-21 start and gauging the trade market for Kawhi Leonard and James Harden each, the Clippers poked around on McDaniels, but were rebuffed, HoopsHype has learned.

item.title: NBA execs believe Magic will eventually choose between Jalen Suggs and Anthony Black
item.description: While the contract of Isaac gives Orlando flexibility to shed salary or use as a potential trade chip, the immediacy of Black’s extension talks will be interesting following Jalen Suggs getting a five-year, $150 million extension, and with Black having comparable statistics to Suggs last season. NBA executives across the league believe Orlando will eventually have to choose between keeping Suggs or Black on the roster long-term due to their incoming salary cap situation.

item.title: RJ Barrett drawing trade interest
item.description: Toronto Raptors swingman RJ Barrett has drawn trade interest in multi-team conversations, league sources told HoopsHype. The Canadian swingman is on an expiring $29.62 million contract this upcoming season. He’s averaged 20.5 points on 49.5 percent shooting from the field and 35.3 percent beyond the arc with 5.9 rebounds and 4.3 assists since joining his hometown Raptors.

item.title: Jazz interested in re-signing Jusuf Nurkic
item.description: The Utah Jazz has expressed interest in re-signing center Jusuf Nurkic, league sources told Hoopshype.

item.title: Sources say other assistant coaching candidates in the …
item.description: Meanwhile, Sean Sweeney’s coaching staff has begun to take shape with HoopsHype reporting the additions of DJ Bakker, Mfon Udofia, and Riley Crean as assistant coaches. Sources say other assistant coaching candidates in the mix for Sweeney’s staff include Joe Prunty, Popeye Jones, Greg Buckner, and Tom Bialaszewski.

item.title: "Definitely helped with [getting] a feel for how this …
item.description: Ivica Zubac won't be flying completely blind in 2026-27, but he'll still be adjusting along the way. His offseason will be important, as will training camp. That's one advantage of getting the trade done in February, Zubac is a member of the Pacers for the entire offseason. Some of the team's assistant coaches, including Jenny Bouckey and Jim Boylen, have been with Zubac in Europe this summer. "Definitely helped with [getting] a feel for how this team wants to play, about the pace, about defensi

item.title: After picks Nos. 5-9, as the NBA Draft order currently …
item.description: Jake Fischer: After picks Nos. 5-9, as the NBA Draft order currently stands, are projected to feature a slew of guards, the next dozen picks have executives around the league preparing for a run on big men.

item.title: Lakers impressed by Braden Smith
item.description: The Lakers spent time in Spain looking at 20-year-old guard Sergio de Larrea, but many NBA scouts see him going later in the first round or even in the second. According to people not authorized to speak publicly, the Lakers were impressed by their workout with Purdue point guard Braden Smith. But he’s on the smaller side (6 feet) and played four years in college, leading scouts to believe his upside is not that high and that he’ll be drafted in the second round.

item.title: Jordan Nwora is staying with Crvena Zvezda despite …
item.description: Jordan Nwora is staying with Crvena Zvezda despite transfer interest from Hapoel Tel Aviv. President Zeljko Drcelic declared that the prolific scorer is not for sale this summer.

item.title: Patrick Mills calls season in Tenerife 'the greatest year of my career'
item.description: Patrick Mills: Accidentally stumbled upon an island in the Atlantic that turned into the greatest year of my career. Thank you to the people of Tenerife for welcoming our family with open arms and sharing the stories, history, and culture that make this island so special. Al golpito. Little by little, this island felt less like a destination and more like a place of belonging. And somewhere in between, there were some pretty special moments on the court too. Ar emir iyen, Tenerife. ❤️ @CB1939Can

You don't like the moment you lost your pride, the biggest game of your career, but you're

item.title: Lakers in the mix for Mitchell Robinson, Robert Williams?
item.description: The Lakers have been linked to all sorts of veteran big men in the forthcoming free agent market as well. They could emerge as a suitor for the Knicks' Mitchell Robinson and the Trail Blazers' Robert Williams III, although sources say both players are very open to remaining in their incumbent roles with the Knicks and Blazers. I'm also told that the Lakers have called the Thunder about swingman Lu Dort's availability.

item.title: The Bucks, incidentally, are VERY much aware of how …
item.description: Barry Jackson: The Bucks, incidentally, are VERY much aware of how much Giannis wants to play in Miami. They seem determined to leave the Heat in a compromised roster position so that the Heat also has a hard time doing what the Bucks couldn't do the past 5 years (build a championship team around him). item.title: Peterson didn’t hesitate in calling James the GOAT
item.description: Peterson recently spoke about his admiration of James, saying that while he hasn’t yet met him, James commenting on his Instagram posts meant so much and that he hopes to have the career longevity of the all-time great, via NBA Future Now on X: Peterson didn’t hesitate in calling James the GOAT while also adding that his favorite team is the Lakers simply because that is who James plays for. That is the case for many fans these days who sometimes have more loyalty towards individual players than

item.title: The Mavericks and Brayden Burries have mutual interest …
item.description: Dallas, though, has been very open, sources say, to moving down the board. We've been told the Mavericks and Brayden Burries have mutual interest at No. 9. But if Burries is not there — and we've already reported he's under legitimate consideration by the Clippers at No. 5 — that could ultimately lead to even more reason for Dallas to slide back.

item.title: One potential target if Dallas were to trade down: …
item.description: One potential target if Dallas were to trade down: Washington big man Hannes Steinbach. Sources say that Steinbach, whose father Burkhard played alongside Mavericks legend Dirk Nowitzki on the German League team in their shared hometown of Wurzburg some 30 years ago, is among the prospects to have worked out for the Mavericks under consideration for the No. 9 pick.

item.title: Atlanta sees great value in Swain at No. 23,
item.description: I've also heard that Atlanta sees great value in Swain at No. 23, but the Hawks have been signaling for some time that they are prepared (and perhaps even prefer) to trade their second pick in the first round after No. 8 for future draft capital. It sounds as though Atlanta will invite external trade interest for that pick until it is actually on the clock to make the selection Tuesday night.

item.title: Nothing has changed, as I said, I will not play this …
item.description: It was previously known that Luka Doncic would not be part of the Slovenian national team in early July, nor would he help Slovenia in the second part of the 2027 World Cup qualifiers in Qatar at the end of August. " Nothing has changed, as I said, I will not play this summer, " he added. Due to a hamstring injury, the Lakers' first star missed the entire North American league playoffs.

item.title: I won't hide it, if you don't win the title, it's a …
item.description: " I won't hide it, if you don't win the title, it's a bad season. We've been unlucky with injuries, myself included, after we played some great basketball in March. It's going to be a long time before next season. I hope it's better for us ." His club teammate, 2.13 m tall American center Jaxson Hayes , recently received Slovenian citizenship. " I wasn't involved in these talks at all. He's a good guy and that's what he is as a player. Otherwise, we have a young team that gives us hope. I want t

item.title: Even when I'm here, I hardly go anywhere, that's the …
item.description: He has a star status in Los Angeles and around the world, which also has a great impact on his private life, which he did not want to talk about in detail, including the breakup with his fiancée Anamarija Goltes . " Even when I'm here, I hardly go anywhere, that's the price for the position I'm in and what I wanted. It's completely different than in Los Angeles, where I feel good ."

item.title: Of course, I enjoy playing golf. There's nothing …
item.description: But he couldn't hide the excitement he found in the game of golf. " Of course, I enjoy playing golf. There's nothing better than spending four hours in nature. But I also choose to play 36 holes, which isn't exactly the best, and I play and enjoy it for eight hours. That's the most beautiful thing ," he said on the platform with the basketball court at the Stožice hall.

item.title: Nick Young: 'Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant was fighting over Finals MVP'
item.description: Nick Young: "Steph and Kevin Durant was fighting over Finals MVP, that's about it. You could tell they both was trying to get it without saying they trying to get it. Kevin Durant was taking it a little easy, I felt like, and Steph wasn't having that good of a game that game. So Kevin Durant just had to turn it up. And I think that's when he won Finals MVP too, after that game. It was a big night for him."

item.title: Nick Young: "Steph is like the good cop to Draymond's …
item.description: Nick Young: "Steph is like the good cop to Draymond's bad cop. You got to have that kind of balance. Being Draymond's being Draymond, Steph will pull you to the side and be like, 'Don't worry about that, just continue to play, things going to work out.' So he's a good dude. item.title: Nick Young on JR Smith in Game 1: "At the moment I …

item.title: Jordan Goodwin to return to Phoenix on three-year, $19 million deal
item.description: Shams Charania: Free agent guard Jordan Goodwin intends to sign a three-year, $19 million deal to return to the Phoenix Suns, with a player option in the third season, sources tell ESPN. Goodwin made the Suns roster out of training camp on a non-guaranteed contract and emerged as a key reserve and culture fit, averaging 8.7 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.2 assists, and a team-high 106 total steals.

item.title: In consecutive days, the Suns land multiyear …
item.description: Shams Charania: In consecutive days, the Suns land multiyear agreements to keep two young guards in Goodwin and Collin Gillespie whom the franchise developed over the last year. Goodwin's agents at Klutch Sports, Shy Saee and Mike George, landed the deal Sunday, a week after free agents became eligible to negotiate with their own teams. Next order of business for the Suns: retaining restricted free agent Mark Williams.

item.title: Hawks, CJ McCollum agree to a one-year, $21 million contract extension
item.description: Shams Charania: Atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum has agreed to a one-year, $21 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a trade kicker, agent Sam Goldfeder of Excel Sports Management tells ESPN. McCollum has been eligible for an extension until June 30 and commits to a new deal that keeps him out of free agency.contract extension with the franchise, plus a trade kicker, agent Sam Goldfeder of Excel Sports Management tells ESPN.

McCollum is now signed through next season.

item.title: Dwyane Wade opens up on mental health struggles after retiring
item.description: Dwyane Wade shared that retiring from basketball — a sport he had played his entire life — took an emotional toll. “Once you retire, that's when, you know … you really go through a moment, a time of depression,” he said. “And it's how you decide to handle that depression which is going to determine your next step because, you know — since I was 5 years old — that's what I did, played basketball. And then I was really good at it. So now you're coming out of this world and … now I got to get anoth

item.description: Wade went on to say that “the first thing” he did when he retired was start therapy, despite the fact that he previously had some resistance to the idea. “I was the Black man that was like, ‘Therapy ain't for me,' ” he explained. However, Wade said he intuitively knew he needed an emotional outlet post-retirement. “Basketball not only was a place where I had so much success … it was also my outlet, you know what I mean? Like, I could scream. I can yell. I can curse. I could, you know — not fight

Started out in the latter part of the first round and now could be a lottery pick. The kind of athletic big that teams want at the 4 in today's game.

item.description: Keith Smith: One note (that likely will not matter) on CJ McCollum's contract being an extension vs a new deal: He's immediately trade-eligible with no waiting period once he's signed. A new contract signed in July would have come with a December 15 trade restriction.

item.title: Lakers looking for an upgrade at the center position
item.description: That’s not to say neither Marcus Smart or Deandre Ayton will be back (both have player options), but team sources have repeatedly talked about an upgrade at the center position. item.title: Lakers were “on the clock” with Dončić right after the …

Dončić is in the prime of his career and was traded away from a roster built to his specifications to compete for NBA titles. And if the Lakers can’t provide that, maybe he looks elsewhere (if anybody should understand that this is business, it’s Dončić).

item.title: Evans has worked out for the Knicks,
item.description: Isaiah Evans, Wing, Duke: Evans can really, really shoot the ball, both stationary and off the move. That’s about it, though. He needs to get stronger to regularly contribute in the NBA. He doesn’t pass well. He’s not a great defender. However, if he’s able to shoot at an elite level in the NBA and be good enough defensively, that’s a rotation piece all NBA teams look for. Evans has worked out for the Knicks, per league sources.

item.title: Wolves keeping Jaden McDaniels?

Center Joan Beringer is also a player the Wolves want to keep because of his size, athleticism and feel for the game. item.description: The list of veterans whom the Wolves have discussed this spring includes the Milwaukee Bucks’ Giannis Antetokounmpo, the Dallas Mavericks’ Kyrie Irving, the New Orleans Pelicans’ Trey Murphy III, the Chicago Bulls’ Josh Giddey, the Boston Celtics’ Derrick White and many more. item.title: Sam Amick and I reported that the Lakers were “on the …
item.description: Sam Amick and I reported that the Lakers were “on the clock” with Dončić right after the end of last season, and nothing I’ve heard from my sources would change that thought process. item.title: Michigan's Dusty May to coach the Mavericks
item.description: Michigan coach Dusty May is finalizing a deal to take the Dallas Mavericks head coaching job, sources told ESPN, an axis-shifting move that significantly alters the college and NBA landscape. item.title: Dusty May is the first college head coach to take an …
item.description: Dusty May is the first college head coach to take an NBA job since former Michigan coach John Beilein took the Cleveland Cavaliers job in 2019. The last to leave college immediately after winning a national title was Kansas' Larry Brown in 1988. Florida's Billy Donovan was the most recent NCAA title-winning coach to leave for the NBA in 2015.

item.title: Wizards front office expected Trae Young to command max salary offers
item.description: The NBA rumor mill, which is often inaccurate, predicted months ago that any new deal between Trae Young and the Wizards would average no more than $40 million annually. But in recent weeks, Wizards decision-makers became convinced that, with the NBA’s new anti-tanking measures compelling more teams to compete, Young was going to command maximum-salary contract offers from other franchises through either a straight free-agent signing or a sign-and-trade proposal.

item.title: For Washington, the difference between signing Young …
item.description: Because the Wizards hold Young’s Bird rights, the Wizards had the latitude to offer Young up to a five-year contract with 8 percent annual raises. But Young’s new four-year deal instead features 5 percent year-over-year raises, the maximum year-over-year raise that any other team could have offered Young as a non-Bird free agent. For Washington, the difference between signing Young to 5 percent raises instead of 8 percent raises will amount to a total savings of $8.9 million over four years.

item.title: Golden Knights owner Bill Foley launches bid for NBA franchise in Las Vegas
item.description: Bill Foley is looking to add another sports franchise to his portfolio. The founder and majority owner of the Vegas Golden Knights announced that he is pursuing the award of an NBA franchise for Las Vegas. Earlier this year, the NBA voted to formally explore expansion, with one of those potential markets including Las Vegas.

item.title: "Las Vegas has earned its place among the great sports …
item.description: "Las Vegas has earned its place among the great sports cities in America, and an NBA team belongs here," Foley said. "We built the Golden Knights into a championship organization from the ground up, and we are prepared to do it again – with the same standard, the same commitment to this community, and the same insistence on winning. We have the market, a proven world-class arena, and a best-in-class organization in place. Our intention is to be ready the day the NBA is ready."

item.title: Hawks are the most active team in discussing trade …
item.description: League sources say the Hawks are the most active team in discussing trade scenarios. They completed a deal with the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday night to acquire Aaron Wiggins into the trade exception they generated when they dealt Luke Kennard to the Los Angeles Lakers at the deadline. Sources have said Atlanta is discussing both trade-up and trade-down scenarios. But it also could just stay here and take the player it wants if he remains on the board.

item.title: Celtics not willing to add multiple firsts for Giannis Antetokounmpo
item.description: Heat Central: The Bucks owners are “split” on which decision to make with a Giannis trade and Boston is NOT willing to add multiple 1st round picks like Miami, per @JakeLFischer “We’re being told there is some type of split faction in MIL right now among the major stakeholders for the Bucks… the Celtics to our understanding, are not willing to offer the same level of multiple years of draft capital that the Miami Heat are” (Via @BleacherReport)

item.title: "Legendary. I feel like will be one of the best, if …
item.description: Oh No He Didn't: Caleb Wilson on how his draft class will be remembered: "Legendary. I feel like will be one of the best, if not the best draft classes ever"

item.title: Rockets willing to listen to offers excluding Amen Thompson
item.description: Rival teams that have contacted the Rockets recently have been informed that 23-year-old Amen Thompson is the only near untouchable on the roster, league sources told Yahoo Sports. Houston isn't actively shopping its All-Stars or other key members, sources said, but is merely expressing more of a willingness to listen than at previous junctures.

item.title: Charlotte, armed with picks Nos. 14 and 18, is …
item.description: Charlotte, armed with picks Nos. 14 and 18, is believed to be exploring avenues to move up, sources said, along with Chicago at No. 15 (which also owns the No. 4 pick) and Memphis at No. 16 (which also owns the 3rd overall selection).

item.title: "No NBA players have texted me this week"
item.description: Oh No He Didn't: AJ Dybantsa ahead of the draft: "No NBA players have texted me this week"

item.title: AJ Dybantsa on his draft class: I think it's going to be one of the most talked about since LeBron's
item.description: Oh No He Didn't: AJ on his draft class: "I think at least 10 of us will probably be still playing...let's say 8 years down the road. I think that's how deep we are but it could be more. I think it's gonna be probably one of the most talked about draft classes since LeBron's I think"

item.title: While the reigning champion New York Knicks assess …
item.description: Jake Fischer: While the reigning champion New York Knicks assess their trade options for picks No. 24 and 31 in this week’s NBA Draft, sources say reserve guard Jose Alvarado has agreed to move the decision date on his $4.5 million player option for 2026-27 from tomorrow, June 22, back to June 26.

item.title: Adjusting these figures slightly, as Young's new …
item.description: Keith Smith: Adjusting these figures slightly, as Young's new contract is reported to start at the 30% max amount of $49.5M: 26-27: $49.5M 27-28: $51.9M 28-29: $54.5M 29-30: $56.9M (player option) Total: $212.85M (matches what Young could have gotten from another team as a FA)

item.title: Today with the fam we treated ourselves to the huge …
item.description: Manu Ginobili: Today with the fam we treated ourselves to the huge pleasure of watching an ARG match in a World Cup for the first time and on top of that, watching the 10 become the all-time leading scorer in World Cups!! What a privilege!!

item.title: Mohamed Diawara plans to sign multi-year deal to stay with Knicks
item.description: Shams Charania: Restricted free agent Mohamed Diawara intends to sign a multiyear, $10-plus million deal to return to the New York Knicks, sources tell ESPN. Diawara -- the No. 51 pick in last year's NBA draft -- was part of the champion Knicks after spending the season on a standard contract.

item.title: This doesn't preclude them, they say, from taking …
item.description: Brian Windhorst: "Speaking to the Wizards today, they are very happy to get Trae Young under contract. This doesn't preclude them, they say, from taking Peterson with the number one pick. Now, whether we believe that or not is a different story."

item.title: And, you know, we kind of talk around it and dance …
item.description: Josh Hart: "No one knows the understand besides y'all that wear the jersey, no one understands the weight that that jersey has sometimes. And, you know, we kind of talk around it and dance around it, but New York is a special place, but there's a lot of pressure when you put that jersey on. So we want to thank you and celebrate you (Carmelo Anthony) a little bit, man, for laying the foundation, but also, you know, talking to us during it."

item.title: @SportsVanessa will serve as ESPN's reporter for …
item.description: Greg Rajan: Rockets sideline reporter @SportsVanessa will serve as ESPN's reporter for Wednesday's second round of the NBA draft. She'll also host the digital "Hoop Streams" show for Tuesday's round 1 on the ESPN app and the network's social platforms.

item.title: Raptors could be interested in Myles Turner?
item.description: A couple of league sources have suggested that the Raptors could be interested in Bucks centre Myles Turner if the Bucks go into fire-sale mode after a potential Antetokounmpo trade.

item.title: It’s expected the Toronto Raptors will announce a …
item.description: It’s expected the Toronto Raptors will announce a multi-year contract extension for head coach Darko Rajakovic early this week, both as a reward for a job well done and a bet that he can continue to develop as a longtime leader of a team that’s trying to transition from "pretty good" to "actually good" and, ideally, much better than that over the life of the deal.

item.title: Per sources, it’s a move that Dick would be open to as …
item.description: The most likely development as the off-season unfolds will be a new address for Gradey Dick, the fourth-year wing who was leapfrogged in the rotation by Ja'Kobe Walter, Jamison Battle and A.J. Lawson in the final weeks of the season. Per sources, it’s a move that Dick would be open to as he looks for a fresh start and a chance to pick up from his promising second season (14.4 points per game with 54 starts) after things went south in Year 3 (six points per game with one start).

item.title: Anthony Davis and his camp have been seeking a max …
item.description: Fullcourtpass: Anthony Davis and his camp have been seeking a max extension, and it’s plausible to consider him a potential trade candidate out of Washington, per @JakeLFischer (h/t @TheDunkCentral)

item.title: GOD, I trusted you at the beginning, and I will …
item.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo: GOD, I trusted you at the beginning, and I will continue to trust you throughout.

item.title: Kyrie Irving is kicking off his latest ANTA Tour this …
item.description: Nick DePaula: Kyrie Irving is kicking off his latest ANTA Tour this week — with a World Tour summer schedule featuring cities throughout Asia and in the US. The Las Vegas and New Jersey dates in July will also include Irving’s “Uncle Drew Circuit” youth basketball tournament games.

item.title: Blazers will be looking to trade for Anthony Davis is he becomes available
item.description: In his latest NBA insider report for Bleacher Report, Jake Fischer announced that the Blazers are open to the possibility of trading for the star big man should the Washington Wizards like to entertain a trade. "Portland, to our understanding, as they have been floating around and poking around in Giannis trade conversations, we've been told that they would look to pivot to Anthony Davis on the trade market," Fischer said. "They obviously have Jaylen Brown interest as well. "We've been told that

item.title: Pelicans have maintained an asking price of MULTIPLE …
item.description: Fullcourtpass: The Pelicans have maintained an asking price of MULTIPLE first-round picks for Trey Murphy or Herb Jones, per @JakeLFischer 6-12 teams have inquired about trading for them

item.title: He (Giannis) is on his way back from the states as of …
item.description: Heat Central: Giannis is on his way back from the states and ready for a trade to Miami or Boston, per @ShamsCharania "At this very hour the MIL Bucks are moving closer and closer to a trade resolution for Giannis.... He (Giannis) is on his way back from the states as of right now. He's ready for a trade whether it's Miami or Boston"

item.title: Those sources were granted anonymity so they could …
item.description: But NCAA and NBA sources who spoke with The Athletic consistently said they believe that May has what it takes to make the leap. Those sources were granted anonymity so they could speak freely, and “modern,” “collaborative” and “adaptable” were all words used to describe May, a Terre Haute, Ind., native. So was the word “kind,” which might seem strange for someone who got his start working as a student manager for the rough-edged Bob Knight at Indiana.

item.title: Duke’s Jon Scheyer was one name the Mavericks heavily …
item.description: The Mavericks interviewed NBA assistant coaches Micah Nori, Royal Ivey and Jama Mahlalelah, league sources said, while also closely examining the college ranks. Duke’s Jon Scheyer was one name the Mavericks heavily considered. In fact, their interest in him pre-dated Ujiri’s arrival, league sources said.

item.title: They have discussed a variety of trade-back scenarios, …
item.description: The Mavericks are expected to go into next season with Flagg and Kyrie Irving as cornerstones. They control the Nos. 9, 30 and 48 selections in this week’s NBA Draft. They have discussed a variety of trade-back scenarios, including one, according to league sources, that would net Dallas the No. 16 pick that Memphis currently controls.

item.title: Carlos Boozer on teams that don't draft his son Cameron: 'They will regret it'
item.description: All these GMs know you. So, when they ask you why should they draft him, and if we don’t, what would you say? Carlos Boozer: If they miss the boat, they will regret it. This kid is a winner. Basically, the one thing about Cam that separates him from everybody else in the draft is that he’s a guy that the rest of the team will galvanize around because he doesn’t cheat the game. Carlos Boozer: I knew that this one was really special, probably like around like sixth grade. We had him with different trainers that were really good with developing skill sets in the backyard. item.description: When Cam gets to the NBA, what lessons have you instilled in him that you know he’s going to take with him wherever he goes? Carlos Boozer: He’s so fundamentally sound. He has a great focus. He’s not going to get sidetracked. A lot of guys, me included, you get to the NBA and you start to get access to stuff that you didn’t have access to. item.title: “But at the end of the day, I’m going to a great …
item.description: “I’m excited just to hear my name get called, walk across that stage,” Cameron Boozer said. “No idea what that feeling is going to be like. You can be nervous, because you just don’t know where you can end up. It’s not really in your hands. “But at the end of the day, I’m going to a great situation, regardless of where I go. And I’m just excited for what the future has in store. It seems to be a lot of fun.”

item.title: Knicks and Diawara are working on eight figure deal to …
item.description: Ian Begley: Mohamed Diawara was certainly going to get significant interest from other teams as a restricted free agent, per league sources. Knicks and Diawara are working on eight figure deal to bring the rookie back to NY. Not done, but all signs pointing to it getting done, sources confirm. Diawara felt welcomed by NY from Day One and was very comfortable with his teammates. So even if another big offer came, NY had an edge. ESPN first reported Diawara deal.

item.title: They can give Mohamed Diawara up to four years, $11.3 …
item.description: Yossi Gozlan: New York Knicks updated salary cap situation. They can give Mohamed Diawara up to four years, $11.3 million with his Non Bird rights. His minimum over four years is $10.6 million. They are still free to go above the second apron by re-signing their own free agents.

item.title: According to Eurohoops sources, Real Madrid has signed …
item.description: According to Eurohoops sources, Real Madrid has signed the new 10-year agreement with EuroLeague Basketball and is set to become a franchise alongside the league’s other shareholder clubs.

item.title: Celtics want to keep Hugo Gonzalez
item.description: Bill Simmons: I’m just gonna say…. I would be absolutely shocked if Hugo was/is thrown into any Giannis trade offer. The entire organization is all-in on him - Stevens prob the most. They could not be higher on him. I genuinely don’t believe he’s involved. Guess we’ll see.

item.title: The Celtics, as Bill says, certainly prefer to keep …
item.description: Marc Stein: The Bucks, as we reported last night, have certainly asked for Hugo. The Celtics, as Bill says, certainly prefer to keep him. Not exactly a make-or-break element but one of the variables that factors into this Boston vs. Miami struggle.

item.title: Since when is a 6’9 wing who plays any role you ask, …
item.description: kuz: Since when is a 6’9 wing who plays any role you ask, guards 1–5, shot almost 50% from the field and cares about defense a ‘throw‑in’? lol

item.title: But he says he’s a film junkie and studies opponent …
item.description: Kevin O'Connor: Darryn Peterson says he didn’t watch much basketball when he was a kid, and it was hard to watch full playoff games this year because he just got a new puppy. But he says he’s a film junkie and studies opponent tendencies.

item.title: To that end, the Nets met with Brown at least three …
item.description: To that end, the Nets met with Brown at least three times — including a workout in Brooklyn and visiting his family in Orlando. “It’s definitely unique,” Brown said of the visit. “Obviously there’s definitely been interest there, as there is in almost every single other team. But yeah, definitely, it made an impact. They got to talk to my mom and my dad. It was a great conversation.”

item.title: Julius Randle heads to Brooklyn in three-team trade
item.description: Shams Charania: Just in: Minnesota is sending Julius Randle and the No. 28 pick in the NBA Draft to the Brooklyn Nets in a three-team trade that sends Nic Claxton to the Chicago Bulls, sources tell ESPN. The Timberwolves will acquire Brooklyn’s No. 33 pick for Randle and No. 28.

item.title: Timberwolves are trading Julius Randle to Brooklyn,
item.description: Jon Krawczynski: The Timberwolves are trading Julius Randle to Brooklyn, sources say

item.title: Timberwolves free up significant salary with the …
item.description: Shams Charania: Timberwolves free up significant salary with the remaining two years of Randle's deal, giving them more flexibility to retain Ayo Dosunmu and use exceptions. Nets acquire a three-time All-Star and two-time All-NBA forward in Randle into their cap space -- plus a first-rounder. Chicago uses part of its space on a talented athletic center, a position of need, with $30 million in room left.

item.title: Timberwolves now have the flexibility to re-sign Ayo …
item.description: Bobby Marks: The Timberwolves now have the flexibility to re-sign Ayo Dosunmu and have available the $15M non tax midlevel and $5.5M biannual exception. Minnesota will also create a $33.3M trade exception.

item.title: Chris Haynes reporting that Celtics are the favorites …
item.description: Barry Jackson: Chris Haynes reporting that Celtics are the favorites to acquire Giannis tonight or tomorrow

item.title: Naz Reid will be the starting power forward for Wolves after Julius Randle trade
item.description: Jon Krawczynski: Naz Reid is going to be the starting power forward for the Minnesota Timberwolves for the first time in his career. This move is a big statement of belief in Reid and Jaden McDaniels to take the next steps in their development.

item.title: Bulls will use $23.1 million of their cap space to …
item.description: Yossi Gozlan: The Bulls will use $23.1 million of their cap space to acquire Nic Claxton. They go from from $54 million in cap space to $30.9 million in room remaining. They would still have the $9.4 million room mid-level to use after. Great business getting him essentially for free.

item.title: This pending trade is essentially a “free agent …
item.description: K.C. Johnson: This pending trade is essentially a “free agent signing” of starting caliber center who has averaged 69 starts over last 4 seasons. Claxton, 27, is career 62.2% shooter and solid lob threat who also averaged 3.7 assists last season. Typically makes good decisions as roll man.

item.title: This move would still leave Bulls with roughly $30M of …
item.description: K.C. Johnson: Nic Claxton has $23M and $21M left on his deal. This move would still leave Bulls with roughly $30M of cap space this summer

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo trade may expand before July 6
item.description: The trade does not include any additional teams -- it is a one-to-one move, sources said -- but both the Heat and Bucks will execute the deal on July 6, which leaves the framework open to see if there are opportunities to expand. Last June, the Phoenix Suns and Houston Rockets agreed to a deal that ultimately increased to a historic seven-team trade.

item.title: The Celtics registered interest in Antetokounmpo at …
item.description: The Bucks seriously negotiated with two finalists in recent weeks: the Heat and Boston Celtics, who were both on Antetokounmpo's list of preferred destinations. The Celtics registered interest in Antetokounmpo at the trade deadline in February, and aggressively pursued him this time around, offering Milwaukee a package featuring 2024 Finals MVP Jaylen Brown and two first-round picks, according to sources.

item.title: Brad Stevens has not actively shopped Brown in trade …
item.description: Celtics president Brad Stevens has not actively shopped Brown in trade talks, sources said, but the franchise has now offered him twice for future Hall of Famers over the past four offseasons. In 2022, Brown was the centerpiece of Boston's proposal to the Brooklyn Nets for Kevin Durant.

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo's camp told Bucks he would not sign a long-term extension with the team
item.description: Sources told ESPN that Antetokounmpo and his agent, Alex Saratsis, consistently informed the Bucks from May 2025 through May 2026 that the franchise legend wanted a trade from the organization because he believed it was best for both sides to part ways. Antetokounmpo's reps informed the Bucks several times over the past 13 months -- including before, during and after the season -- that he would not sign another long-term extension with the team, according to sources. The Bucks made the decision

item.title: Kasparas Jakucionis was Miami's version of Boston's …
item.description: Jake Fischer: Kasparas Jakucionis was Miami's version of Boston's Hugo Gonzalez hang-up. Had been hearing all day the Heat did not want to part with the Illinois product on top of their Herro-Ware-Jacquez-No. 13 structure. That's an All-Star guard, three recent first-round picks still on rookie deals, a second lottery pick in tomorrow's loaded draft class, plus two more future firsts and a swap... It's really a sizable haul for Giannis Antetokounmpo. Compared to Jaylen Brown and two first-round

item.title: I can confirm that Heat has been informed by the Bucks …
item.description: Barry Jackson: I can confirm that Heat has been informed by the Bucks that they're getting Giannis. Cautious optimism pays off lol. Miami is exactly where Giannis preferred to be, someone who works for him reiterated again today.

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo will be eligible starting on …
item.description: Bobby Marks: Giannis Antetokounmpo will be eligible starting on January 6 to sign an extension for: 4 years/$275M if he opts-out 3 years/$214M if he opts-in The opt-in is slightly more lucrative

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo heads to Miami in six player deal
item.description: Shams Charania: BLOCKBUSTER: The Milwaukee Bucks are trading franchise icon Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Miami Heat for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, 3 first-round picks (including No. 13), 1 pick swap and 1 second-rounder, sources tell ESPN.

item.title: Heat are sending to Milwaukee unprotected …
item.description: Shams Charania: The Heat are sending to Milwaukee unprotected first-rounders in 2031 and 2033 along with No. 13, a pick swap in 2030 and a 2033 second-rounder, according to sources. The trade does not include any additional teams -- it is a one-to-one move, sources said -- but both the Heat and Bucks will execute the deal on July 6, which leaves the framework open to see if there are opportunities to expand.

item.title: Heat will bring Bobby Portis in via the Duncan …
item.description: Keith Smith: The Heat will bring Bobby Portis in via the Duncan Robinson TPE they have. Miami will be hard-capped at the first apron after completing this deal, which will be in July after the league year changes over.

item.title: Ayo Dosunmu will sign five-year deal to remain in Minnesota
item.description: Shams Charania: Free agent guard Ayo Dosunmu intends to sign a five-year, $112 million contract to return to the Minnesota Timberwolves, with a player option in the fifth season, sources tell ESPN. Timberwolves made it a major priority to lock in Dosunmu after his tremendous postseason.

item.title: Dosunmu’s agents, Mike Lindeman and Jeff Schwartz of …
item.description: Shams Charania: Dosunmu’s agents, Mike Lindeman and Jeff Schwartz of Excel Sports Management, worked with Timberwolves executives on Monday night to land the long-term commitment. Dosunmu and Anthony Edwards gained a chemistry after his arrival from Chicago in February.

item.title: Wolves not interested in Ja Morant
item.description: Jon Krawczynski: The Wolves have not been in the Ja Morant mix. Decision was made to look elsewhere for backcourt help

item.title: Bulls are trading Mo Gueye to Minnesota, sources say, …
item.description: Jake Fischer: The Bulls are trading Mo Gueye to Minnesota, sources say, to complete the three-team deal that sends Julius Randle and No. 28 in tomorrow’s NBA Draft to Brooklyn for No. 33, and reroutes Nic Claxton into Chicago’s cap space in the new league year. Gueye’s salary is non-guaranteed for 2026-27.

item.title: They got Gueye on an end-of-season, non-guaranteed …
item.description: Joel Lorenzi: Bulls had a few options here to make trade legal (cash, top-55 protected future pick, etc). They got Gueye on an end-of-season, non-guaranteed deal in April, and they get Claxton without digging into assets.

item.title: Bucks didn't want to risk Jaylen Brown wanting out of Milwaukee?
item.description: Kevin O'Connor: Sources say Bucks owner Jimmy Haslem was a driving force in taking the Heat deal for Giannis Antetokounmpo over Boston’s offer. Haslem didn’t want to risk Jaylen Brown wanting out of Milwaukee in a year after dealing with Giannis and Myles Garrett trade demands. Haslem wanted certainty, and the Miami deal provided more of that with more total assets in return to Milwaukee.

item.title: The Bucks clear $20 million in the current two-team …
item.description: ‪Yossi Gozlan‬: The Bucks clear $20 million in the current two-team Giannis Antetokounmpo trade framework. They'd create a massive $25.5 million trade exception, which could grow if they expand the trade. It would be useful for taking on bad salaries with draft picks to add to their surplus.

item.title: The Heat are effectively out of first-round picks they …
item.description: ‪Yossi Gozlan‬: The Heat are effectively out of first-round picks they could trade. They could trade their 2029 first-round pick on the condition that their 2027 first-round pick (top-14 protected) conveys to Charlotte. They could try to regain control of it in a trade with the Hornets.

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo was open to signing an extension with Heat, Celtics and Timberwolves before trade
item.description: Chris Haynes: Sources: The 3 teams Giannis Antetokounmpo was open to signing an extension with: Miami, Boston and Minnesota. The Heat land a foundational piece and now have the attention of top players searching for a new home.

item.title: They can re-sign Norman Powell up to any amount with …
item.description: ‪Yossi Gozlan‬: This Heat roster needs shooting. They can re-sign Norman Powell up to any amount with his Bird rights and even extend him now. They'll need to reduce their payroll to create space to re-sign him. They could also use more flexibility to open up the full $15M mid-level.

item.title: The Heat will bring Bobby Portis in via the Duncan …
item.description: ‪KeithSmithNBA‬: The Heat will bring Bobby Portis in via the Duncan Robinson TPE they have. Miami will be hard-capped at the first apron after completing this deal, which will be in July after the league year changes over.

item.title: If Andrew Wiggins opts into $30 M or opts out to sign …
item.description: Barry Jackson: If Andrew Wiggins opts into $30 M or opts out to sign multiyear deal with Miami instead - and if Norman Powell re-signs - that's a rotation of Giannis, Bam, Mitchell, Powell, Wiggins, with Larsson, Bobby Portis and player/players acquired through 3 different exceptions. Pretty, pretty good.

item.title: Ayo Dosunmu's deal comes in around $22 million per …
item.description: ‪Chris Hine‬: Ayo Dosunmu's deal comes in around $22 million per year, higher than I think a lot of folks thought it might. One thing about the Connelly era -- a few more million than perceived isn't much for him to haggle over if he thinks you're a part of the core long term.

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo is the first multi-time MVP …
item.description: Jorge Sierra: FWIW: Giannis Antetokounmpo is the first multi-time MVP winner traded away since Moses Malone.

item.title: The Bucks go from having one of the most dire draft …
item.description: ‪Yossi Gozlan‬: The Bucks go from having one of the most dire draft pick situations to a slight surplus of first-round picks, mostly in the 2030s. The 2030 swap with the Heat could potentially offset the swap they already owe to the Trail Blazers. They could really use more second-round picks.

item.description: Brian Windhorst: I think had Steve Kerr not resigned in Golden State, I think Dusty May would have been on the Warrior short list. I think he was on the short list a couple of other places and he was clearly on the short list for the Mavericks.

item.title: Timberwolves not targeting Ja Morant
item.description: The Wolves are not pursuing Memphis point guard Ja Morant, according to team sources, but will continue to canvas the league for other possibilities.

item.title: The NBA vultures are swirling around Ant …
item.description: Brian Windhorst: My question is what's Anthony Edwards thinking? item.title: Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma trade candidates for Bucks?
item.description: With Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis gone, all eyes turn to holdovers Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma as trade candidates for the Bucks. Turner has always known that if Antetokounmpo was ever traded, he’d be a strong trade candidate, HoopsHype has learned. During his Pacers tenure, Turner was linked to the Hornets, Pelicans, and Lakers in trade rumors at various points. Those teams could all make sense now, and possibly the Celtics. Turner, 30, is still owed $83.55 million, including a player

item.title: Elsewhere, within league circles, there was palpable …
item.description: Elsewhere, within league circles, there was palpable chatter about the Pistons hoping to get involved in the Antetokounmpo trade to land Tyler Herro, while dangling assets such as Isaiah Stewart, Ron Holland, Duncan Robinson, and draft compensation, league sources told HoopsHype. In addition, the Los Angeles Lakers were linked with trade interest in Kel’el Ware over the past couple of days, sources said.

item.title: If any deal with Detroit ever came to fruition, expect …
item.description: Will the Pistons make another run at Herro, who’s currently set to join his hometown Bucks? Or will Detroit attempt to pivot by making a run at Norman Powell in free agency or via trade for Trey Murphy III, whom they’ve expressed interest in? If any deal with Detroit ever came to fruition, expect Pelicans executive Troy Weaver to insist on reuniting with Stewart, one of his favorite players from his Pistons tenure.

item.title: Julius Randle excited to join Brooklyn Nets
item.description: Julius Randle is excited to join the Nets and wants to be in Brooklyn, league sources told HoopsHype. After coming to New York amid a rebuilding situation, Randle evolved into a three-time All-Star and two-time All-NBA forward who helped the crosstown rival Knicks reach consecutive Eastern Conference Semifinals appearances before being dealt to Minnesota as part of the Karl-Anthony Towns trade. Randle is owed $33.33 million for the upcoming season and has a $35.80 million player option for the 2

item.title: Nets wanted to open up more time for Day’Ron Sharpe after Nic Claxton trade
item.description: In addition to moving up five spots into the late first round of the draft, another factor in the decision to trade Nic Claxton was the opportunity to free up more playing time for center Day’Ron Sharpe, sources told HoopsHype. Sharpe, the longest-tenured Net going into his sixth season at just 24 years old, impressed Nets brass last season and was lauded by coach Jordi Fernandez for his rebounding prowess. Sharpe is currently penciled in as Brooklyn’s starting center.

item.title: Warriors have discussed No. 11 pick to Pelicans for Trey Murphy
item.description: Golden State has also been one of many interested suitors in New Orleans Pelicans forward Trey Murphy III, and the two teams have discussed concepts involving the No. 11 pick, league sources told HoopsHype. As previously reported by HoopsHype, the Pelicans have searched for a trade into the lottery and are targeting a player. Nate Ament has been mentioned as one potential candidate for the Pelicans. Before this past trade deadline, several teams, including the Warriors, Pistons, Pacers, Hawks, T

item.title: Warriors, Hornets discussed picks swap
item.description: The Warriors have talked with the Charlotte Hornets about the possibility of swapping draft picks, with Golden State’s No. 11 pick going to Charlotte for Nos. 14 and 18, contingent on certain players being on the board, league sources told HoopsHype. Charlotte has signaled a willingness to move up in the draft, seemingly to leapfrog Oklahoma City, and executives across the league are wondering which player the Hornets could be targeting.

item.description: HH: With this young core and picks No. 3 and 16, where do you see this team’s trajectory? Cedric Coward: 'I see a team that’s trying to develop talent where we can compete with the Spurs, the Thunder, and teams of that caliber that are championship-level teams. For me, I can focus on what I do on the court on a day-to-day basis and how I treat my own work in terms of making sure I’m on top of it and then that will trickle down to helping me be a leader and making sure they’re putting in their ow

item.description: HH: How would you describe Ja Morant, and what could be next for his future? Coward: 'He’s one of my favorite teammates I’ve ever been around. He’s just a standup guy. He’s one of them dudes. When we had the ice storm, he offered to pay for my groceries. I declined it, but the offer was just who he is. He always wants to take care of people. He took care of me as a rookie in certain situations. He’s a good person to be around. He’ll joke around with you. Usually, when you go to teams with supers

item.title: Anthony Edwards still committed to Minnesota
item.description: Everyone wants to know what Anthony Edwards thinks. Multiple sources close to Edwards dismissed the chatter as just that. One said there was no truth to any of it. Another reiterated Edwards and his team love Minnesota, and they think being here, in this location with this franchise is the “ideal” situation.

item.title: Edwards wants to remain a part of a highly competitive …
item.description: Yes, Edwards wants to remain a part of a highly competitive team that is capable of winning playoff series and contending for championships. But there is a faith in the team and in President of Basketball Operations Tim Connelly to do what’s necessary to ensure that vision now and into the future.

item.title: Adam Silver: NBA targeting expansion for the 2028-29 season
item.description: NBA commissioner Adam Silver just put a date on when a potential new Seattle Sonics franchise would begin play should the league decide to award an NBA expansion team to the Emerald City. “If we expand, at least, we’re thinking ’28-29 season,” Silver said Tuesday in an interview on The Dan Patrick Show.

item.title: “The only two cities, at the moment, we’re looking at …
item.description: The 2028-29 season has been speculated as the target should the NBA decide to expand. The NBA Board of Governors approved in March to explore expansion in two specific cities: Seattle and Las Vegas. “The only two cities, at the moment, we’re looking at are Las Vegas and Seattle,” Silver continued to Patrick. “We haven’t had a vote on it, it’s not a foregone conclusion, but we’re in the process of talking to groups that are interested in getting an expansion team in those two cities.”

item.title: Silver also said that if the NBA expands by two to 32 …
item.description: Silver maintained that that the NBA could decide to add two, one or no teams at all at this juncture. “We’re currently looking at two teams, but what we’ve said is it’s possible we won’t expand at all, and we could expand to just one market. But we’re officially looking at both those markets right now,” Silver said. Silver also said that if the NBA expands by two to 32 teams, “we’ll want to likely even out the conferences, so there will be some movement then.”

item.title: DeMar DeRozan expected to be waived and stretched if not traded by Kings
item.description: In the midst of a rebuild and over the first apron, barring an unexpected trade, the Sacramento Kings are expected to waive-and-stretch forward DeMar DeRozan, HoopsHype has learned. DeRozan’s $25.74 million expiring contract is only guaranteed for $10 million, which can be stretched over the next three seasons. Should DeRozan enter free agency as expected, the Los Angeles Clippers are expected to have interest in the California native, HoopsHype has learned.

item.title: Kings unlikely to pursue Ja Morant, plan to draft point guard
item.description: With the Kings projected to take a point guard with the No. 7 pick in the NBA Draft, the chances of the franchise pursuing Ja Morant going forward are unlikely, HoopsHype has learned. This past season, the Kings were willing to acquire Morant if they were incentivized, but Memphis was uninterested in giving up draft compensation to move Morant, a two-time All-Star.

item.title: NBA executives wondering if Norman Powell will leave Heat after Giannis Antetokounmpo trade
item.description: A few executives who spoke with HoopsHype believe Miami’s All-Star guard Norman Powell could now be a candidate to leave the Heat, and the Detroit Pistons are among the teams who’ll be trying to pry him from South Beach, league sources told HoopsHype. Andrew Wiggins has a $30.17 million player option for the upcoming season. Executives are waiting to see if Wiggins will exercise his option or decline it with the intention of signing a new multi-year deal with Miami, or if he’ll consider a new de

item.title: Becky Hammon on Jalen Brunson: 'All he did was prove history wrong'
item.description: Madeline Kenney: Becky Hammon on Jalen Brunson leading the Knicks to a championship: “Jalen, all he did was prove history wrong, he proves he's an outlier, so you can put his name next to Steph Curry and Isiah Thomas, and I thought he played brilliantly, especially down the stretch. I mean, he was that 1A dude, but like, apologize, I'm never gonna apologize for having an opinion, that's what ESPN pays me for.”

item.title: Bucks plan to keep Kel'el Ware for now
item.description: Jake Fischer: I do believe Milwaukee has tried to package Nos. 10 and 13 to move up in tonight's first round, but I don't believe there's going to be any trades in the top-10. Sources say the Bucks, at this point, plan to keep Kel'el Ware, despite interest from rival teams like the Lakers. Milwaukee coveted Ware and Kasparas Jakučionis in their recent drafts. The Bucks also value Tyler Herro, sources say, and don't necessarily plan to move him, while Milwaukee will field offers for the All-Star

So, Trey is going to have a lot of suitors, and I think that could be a draft-night deal. “There was even a scenario floating around with Trey going to the [Atlanta] Hawks in a deal

item.description: I believe that both Washington's Hannes Steinbach and Michigan's Morez Johnson Jr., in addition to Mara, will all be off the board in the top 15. I've been hearing that the Bulls, who hold No. 15, could well be Johnson's floor for some time.

item.description: Sources say that the Hawks and Mavericks both visited Ament last weekend in Memphis, where he was completing his pre-draft preparations.

Philon told me that the Bucks were the one team he worked out for multiple times and I've heard from multiple sources with knowledge of the Bucks' thinking that they are quite high on the Alabama point guard.

I don't know when the most important person in the summertime was the trainer and not the player. I know y'all are going to be like, 'Bron, we ain't seen no five-on-five clips of you lately.' Yeah, and you ain't."

item.description: LeBron James to Steve Nash: "The 96 draft, besides you guys being one of the greatest drafts of all time, is that Slam cover shoot that you guys did. I had that in my room when I stayed in Spring Hills, it was on my wall with all you guys there."

item.description: Myles Turner on dealing with constant NBA trade rumors: "I'm so numb to it now. At the very beginning of my career, I was in a trade rumor every single offseason. I had my bags packed twice. I thought at one point in my career I was going to be traded to Boston for Gordon Hayward and I thought I literally was ready to go and then that fell through at the last second. And then I also thought I was going to be traded to the Lakers for a while. So I'm so numb to it now, if it happens it happens and

item.title: Myles Turner: "I've been with my girlfriend for four …
item.description: Myles Turner: "I've been with my girlfriend for four years now and I tell all the time like my life, my career changed when she into my life. It changed my mindset, it changed my mentality. I had the most success I've had in my career with her by my side."

item.title: Myles Turner: "My parents, they're my everything, man. …
item.description: Myles Turner: "My parents, they're my everything, man. They have supported me through and through no matter what decisions I've made in life and they have helped me immensely. They've exemplified what it means like to be parents and to get me to this level. My mom emptied her retirement fund to fund like my AAU. My dad worked the night shift, so I barely saw him during the day, but if I had a game he would sneak out of work, get someone to cover his shift and watch."

item.title: The Dallas Mavericks today announced the appointment …
item.description: The Dallas Mavericks today announced the appointment of Dusty May as the franchise's new head coach. May joins the Mavericks after leading the University of Michigan to the 2026 NCAA National Championship. Widely regarded as one of the sport's premier program builders and player developers, May has earned a reputation for creating winning cultures, maximizing talent, and leading teams to sustained success.

item.title: "We set out to find a leader who embodies the values …
item.description: "We set out to find a leader who embodies the values we want to define our organization," said Dallas Mavericks President of Basketball Operations Masai Ujiri. "Dusty has won at every stage of his career because of his ability to build. He develops players, creates accountability, and brings people together around a shared standard of excellence. His work ethic is extraordinary, and his teams consistently reflect his values. When you study his journey, you see someone who has earned every opport

item.title: “I am honored to join the Dallas Mavericks …
item.description: “I am honored to join the Dallas Mavericks organization," said May. "This is one of the most respected franchises in professional sports, with passionate fans, a talented roster, and a clear commitment to building a championship organization. I am grateful to Patrick Dumont, Masai Ujiri, and the Mavericks organization for this opportunity, and I look forward to helping bring another championship to the city of Dallas."

But I am told here, as we are hours away from the NBA draft, the Boston Celtics have started to listen, engage and discuss trades around Jaylen Brown. Sources tell me the Celtics are speaking to teams right now about Jaylen Brown. In 2022, the Celt

The Clippers have been in this position before with Kawhi Leonard. When you go into the final year of your deal, you want to know as a veteran player, you are either going to get an extension or not, and Kawhi Leonard is at that point in his career. So whatever happens tonight, I don't think the draft is necessarily dependent on Kawhi Leonard's f

item.title: Caleb Wilson on mock drafts: 'I don't pay attention to it'
item.description: Caleb Wilson on mock draft: “No, I don’t pay attention to it. I feel like whatever God wants me to do, he’s going to do it for me. He’s going to put me where I need to be to succeed. Honestly, it’s all noise. Once I get drafted tomorrow, I get on the flight and it’s time to hoop. I’m not really thinking about where I’m going to be. I’m just thinking about having the opportunity to play at the next level.”

item.title: “Kind of just going in blind. Just wherever, whoever …
item.description: Do you have an idea of your range, or are you going in blind and getting surprised? Allen Graves: “Kind of just going in blind. Just wherever, whoever wants to take a chance on the kid, that's where I'll be. I don't have any preferences or anything like that. Just really grateful to be here, really grateful to be having an opportunity like this and sitting here before y'all, just taking it in one day at a time.”

item.title: Really grateful we get to be here and doing this …
item.description: Allen Graves: “My favorite prospect in this draft, I’m going to go shout out Louisiana, Chris [Cenac]. Louisiana boys. I played against him growing up in high school and everything, so just shout out to him. Really grateful we get to be here and doing this together from Louisiana, just putting on for the boot.”

item.description: Cameron Carr: “My favorite prospect in this draft, I’m going to say Chris [Cenac]. I played against him this year, and I’ve gotten to see him two times and what he has to bring to the table. I’m excited for everything that guy has in store.”

He’s a freak athlete, he’s been jumping out of the gym since we were kids. Crazy wingspan, man. He’s been shooting well. I think he has potential to be a longtime NBA player, great in the league.”

item.title: Unrivaled and Project B have similar schedules during …
item.description: The split decision underscores a new reality in women’s basketball: Two winter leagues are battling each other for top WNBA talent. Unrivaled and Project B have similar schedules during the WNBA offseason, making players unlikely to participate in both leagues, though both have worked around players’ WNBA and national team obligations.

item.title: Project B also confirmed to FOS this week that its …
item.description: he league has announced a slew of its own celebrity investors, including WNBA legends Candace Parker and Lauren Jackson, and tennis stars Novak Djokovic and Sloane Stephens. The Financial Times reported in February 2025 that Project B was backed by Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund, but the company told FOS in November that Saudi Arabia is not a financial backer. Project B also confirmed to FOS this week that its relationship with Saudi events company Sela has ended.

item.description: ESPN NBA reporter Tim Bontemps is in advanced talks to join the Atlanta Hawks’ front office, sources told Front Office Sports. A deal has not been finalized, one source said. Spokespeople for the Hawks and ESPN declined to comment.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard says his stoicism comes from playing with the Spurs
item.description: The stoicism, it turns out, has an origin story. “I think it started off just being on the Spurs,” he says, “just seeing the older vets and how they carried themselves and what they wanted their players to act like on the floor.” The Spurs, under Gregg Popovich, famously ran one of the most understated franchises in professional sports — a culture shaped in no small part by Tim Duncan, who won five championships and retired without ever seeming particularly interested in being celebrated for it.

item.title: The understatement makes me laugh. Because a few …
item.description: Instead, he figured it out himself — through observation, repetition, and what turns out to have been a surprisingly intense hatred of losing. “I just cared about winning a lot,” he says. The understatement makes me laugh. Because a few minutes later he casually admits that he used to cry after losses. Not occasionally. Regularly. “Soon as the game over, if we lose, I’ll just start crying,” he says. Then he laughs. “Like, damn, we lost. I thought you supposed to win every game.” For all the myth

item.title: “Health,” he says, without a pause. “You can’t do …
item.description: But when I ask him what he considers the greatest luxury in life, his answer reframes the entire conversation. “Health,” he says, without a pause. “You can’t do nothing without health. As soon as somebody gets sick, they’re just in a bed, or you’re told you can’t do certain things.” Then he goes somewhere more personal: “Whoever it is — your loved ones — you want them to be able to walk, run, talk, spend time with you.”

item.title: “So if somebody was an NBA player or college player …
item.description: When I ask him what he wishes somebody had told him at twelve years old, the answer comes immediately. “I wish I just had a foundation or somebody that was close to some type of college or NBA team,” he says. “It was kind of like learn as I go. You know, being young, being in Moreno Valley… dad’s far away. Not really in basketball like that.” Suddenly the courts make more sense. So do the free leagues he is building in Moreno Valley and the opportunities he is trying to create for kids coming up

item.title: "He's a guy who really cares for your well-being, not …

He puts away all that stuff aside and steps in like a father-figure role and really cares."

item.title: He's gonna set the standard, but he's also going to …

He's gonna set the standard, but he's also going to follow the standard as well. He's not just gonna say something & do the opposite. He's a great guy. He wants to put his players in the right positions to do well."

He likes to go to work and then return to his home with his family and friends unbothered, and that is exactly what he is allowed to do.

As soon as the Timberwolves were eliminated by San Antonio in the second round of the playoffs last month, front office personnel from other teams started to check in with me, wondering about Edwards’ patience with the Timberwolves’ direction. The game is the game.

item.title: “I’m not going to worry about a GM who’s really good …
item.description: It was around then, Dolan said, that he had an epiphany. “I’m not going to worry about a GM who’s really good at strategy,” he recalled deciding. “What I need is somebody who’s the best collector of talent.” That led him to Rose, who fit the bill as one of the most powerful agents in sports and had spent decades cultivating relationships around the NBA. It was an outside-of-the-box hire, to be sure, but it gave the Knicks a proven dealmaker who could lure winning players to the Garden.

item.title: Adam Silver reiterated his desire for the NBA to …
item.description: Speaking on The Dan Patrick Show, Adam Silver reiterated his desire for the NBA to become “more NFL-like” and said the Spurs-Knicks Finals this spring was the ultimate indicator that the small-market vs. big-market “storyline” is in decline. “The goal over time has been, and I’ve said it, to be more NFL-like. Where you believe your team has a shot,” Silver said.

item.title: Adam Silver: “Maybe not every single season, but your …
item.description: Adam Silver: “Maybe not every single season, but your view is, regardless of the market size, if your team is well-managed, if you have a little bit of luck in there, you have a good chance to be in the playoffs and potentially be the champion. And so I think what we’ve seen is societal changes; I think that nobody’s going to say that Victor Wembanyama in San Antonio can’t get global attention because it’s a smaller market.”

item.title: Coach May told me that among his reasons for leaving …
item.description: “Moving to the NBA is an opportunity for Dusty to further elevate his career. We wish him all best,” Grasso said. “His departure, however, is a bellwether of college athletics. Our current system is in dire need of clarity and equitable reform. Coach May told me that among his reasons for leaving were uncertainties and pressures involving the transfer portal and NIL support for student-athletes. He and I agree that the future of college sports is headed in the wrong direction.”

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo was 'genuinely torn' between wanting to be traded or stay in Milwaukee
item.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo was genuinely torn, multiple sources close to him say. Between loyalty and love of a city that had embraced him as a skinny kid from Greece 13 years ago, and his desire to compete for more championships with a franchise that had exhausted all its resources to try to do that for him. Those contradictory forces had swirled for years.

item.title: Horst had canvassed the league for months, fielding …
item.description: Horst had canvassed the league for months, fielding offers and presenting them to his front office and ownership group, then getting feedback from Antetokounmpo's camp as to whether he'd be willing to extend his contract with those teams. At least four strong bids had died on the vine after Antetokounmpo rejected them, multiple sources with knowledge of them say.

item.title: But by then, the Bucks had their answer, multiple …
item.description: THE BUCKS WERE pressing up against the deadline co-owner Jimmy Haslam had set a month earlier. During a news conference to introduce new coach Taylor Jenkins and sitting alongside Horst, Haslam had made a declaration: The Bucks would have Antetokounmpo's future settled by draft night. Either he would agree to sign an extension to remain with Milwaukee -- or he'd be traded. But by then, the Bucks had their answer, multiple sources with knowledge of the situation say.
