item.title: Several team sources voiced to ESPN a guiding ethos of …
item.description: For half a decade, the Bucks were one of the most successful franchises in the league, leading the NBA in winning percentage (.686) across the regular season and playoffs from 2018 to 2023. Several team sources voiced to ESPN a guiding ethos of the organization through the years: Teams don't willingly trade superstars, especially in a small market such as Milwaukee. It's why the Bucks had made every attempt, through multiple roster iterations, to build championship-level teams with Antetokounmpo

item.title: Antetokounmpo and his reps expressed to Bucks …
item.description: Later that summer, Antetokounmpo and his reps expressed to Bucks management their concerns over the roster, and asked the team to explore a trade to the New York Knicks. Talks stalled.

item.title: In Miami and Boston, however, sleep was hard to come …
item.description: HORST SLEPT WELL Sunday night and longer than he usually does, relieved to be on the other side of the most consequential decision of his professional life. In Miami and Boston, however, sleep was hard to come by. Both franchises believed they had a great chance of landing Antetokounmpo, according to team sources, but they were paralyzed until a final decision had been made.

The final offer for Ball was prepared and sent to owners Marc Lore and Alex Rodriguez for review and approval early Thursday morning, according to multiple team sources that spoke on the condition of anonymity because the trade has not been officially announced.

item.title: “We needed a guy like LaMelo to make everybody …
item.description: Ball averaged 20.1 points, 7.1 assists and 4.8 rebounds last season. There are questions about his decision-making and the seriousness with which he takes the game, but the Wolves love his size, shot creation and playmaking. Maybe even more importantly, the Hornets were 11.6 points per 100 possessions better on offense with Ball on the floor last season, per Cleaning The Glass. item.title: Anthony Edwards has long admired LaMelo Ball's game
item.description: Ball’s ability to initiate offense, shoot 3-pointers at a high volume and see over the top of the defense with his 6-foot-7 frame to find open shooters is exactly what the Wolves were missing. Ball, who was the No. 3 pick in the same 2020 draft class that saw Edwards chosen No. 1, is also just 24. He fits with the timeline of a young core that is tip-toeing into its prime, and he arrives with the tacit approval of Edwards, who has long admired Ball’s game, sources said.

item.title: “He makes Ant better, Jaden (McDaniels) better, Rudy …
item.description: “He makes Ant better, Jaden (McDaniels) better, Rudy and Joan (Beringer) better,” one team source said. “How many other players in the league would make your three best players better without getting in their way?”

And I just remember watching like, 'Damn, Michael Jordan this good? This game boring.' And I just went outside and started hooping. It was Game 3, his last title. They beat them badly. And I was just

item.title: Even without extension talks, Nikola Jokic has reiterated his desire to stay long-term in Denver
item.description: Despite the possibility of Nikola Jokic holding off on extension talks for now, per The Stein Line, Jokic has reiterated a desire to stay long-term in Denver in recent talks, league sources told HoopsHype. If Jokic waits until next summer, he’s eligible for an additional year on an extension, which should be noted.

item.title: Jaylen Brown trade suitors: Blazers, Raptors, Nuggets, Nets, Hornets, Hawks, Clippers
item.description: Brown has drawn trade interest from various teams across the league, including the Portland Trail Blazers, Toronto Raptors, Denver Nuggets, Brooklyn Nets, Charlotte Hornets, Atlanta Hawks, and Los Angeles Clippers, league sources told HoopsHype.

item.title: Pelicans, Rockets, Magic not in the mix for Jaylen Brown
item.description: Other teams, such as the New Orleans Pelicans, Houston Rockets, and Orlando Magic, who’ve been loosely linked to Brown, have been described as not in the mix.

item.title: Deni Avdija was not on the table in trade talks for …
item.description: Trail Blazers All-Star forward Deni Avdija was not on the table in trade talks for Antetokounmpo, and he remains off the table in Brown discussions as of now, league sources told HoopsHype. Portland’s other young players, such as Scoot Henderson and Shaedon Sharpe, are considered available. With Boston considering center upgrades and needing to replace Brown’s position if he’s traded, Portland’s Donovan Clingan and 2025 All-Defensive forward Toumani Camara would both be coveted by Boston. Howeve

item.title: The Nuggets have considered a major roster shakeup, …
item.description: The Nuggets have considered a major roster shakeup, with the franchise willing to listen to offers for anyone other than Nikola Jokic. We have a full outline in the next section of this story on all the Denver trade chatter surrounding its core.

item.title: Celtics still interested in Naz Reid after trade to Hornets
item.description: Reid once again was brought up in talks for Brown after joining the Hornets, HoopsHype has learned. Charlotte has also gauged the trade market value of forward Miles Bridges, who’s on an expiring $22.83 million deal. His salary would be needed to make any Brown trade work with Charlotte. With that said, exploratory talks with the Hornets have cooled.

item.title: The Pistons were linked with interest in free agent …
item.description: Regarding other potential acquisitions, the Pistons were linked with interest in free agent Norman Powell and Kawhi Leonard as a trade suitor. However, that chatter has lessened over the past few days following the Joe acquisition and rumblings that Leonard wouldn’t want to extend with Detroit within league circles.

item.title: Bulls to pursue Norman Powell?
item.description: The Chicago Bulls are among the teams expected to have interest in Powell as free agency nears, league sources told HoopsHype. The 33-year-old guard is a career 39.6 percent three-point shooter. The Detroit Pistons have also been linked to Powell as a potential suitor. Yet, it remains to be seen how the acquisition of Isaiah Joe could impact Detroit’s pursuit of Powell.

item.title: Herro is on an expiring $33 million deal and is …
item.description: Heading into the upcoming season, Herro is on an expiring $33 million deal and is expected to continue to draw trade interest, with many executives around the league curious if Milwaukee will eventually trend more towards a full rebuild or maintain a competitive team with the players acquired for Antetokounmpo.

item.title: Jalen Duren seeking close to $40 million per year?
item.description: With that said, the Pistons have maintained a strong desire to keep their 22-year-old, All-NBA center. Fellow All-NBA selection, Cade Cunningham, also wants Duren back, according to league sources. Within league circles, there’s a belief that Duren is seeking close to $40 million annually, or roughly 25 percent of the NBA’s salary cap. Ultimately, multiple NBA executives who spoke with HoopsHype project Duren to remain with the Pistons and land somewhere around the mid-30s annually once the smo

item.title: Aaron Gordon has drawn trade interest from Blazers; Celtics have kept tabs
item.description: Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon was considered among the contingency plans for the Heat if the franchise didn’t land Giannis Antetokounmpo via trade, league sources told HoopsHype. Similarly, the Portland Trail Blazers have expressed trade interest in Gordon should they not land Jaylen Brown, their preferred target, HoopsHype has learned. Ironically, the Celtics have also kept tabs on Gordon from afar.

item.title: Cam Johnson has drawn trade interest from Lakers, Celtics, Heat, Clippers, Magic
item.description: Meanwhile, as the Nuggets navigate getting below the second apron, sharpshooting forward Cam Johnson has drawn trade interest from several teams, including the Los Angeles Lakers, Boston Celtics, Miami Heat, Los Angeles Clippers, and Orlando Magic, league sources told HoopsHype. The 30-year-old forward shot career-highs from the field (.480) and beyond the arc (.430), and is on an expiring $23.06 million contract for the upcoming season.

item.title: Cavs, 76eres, Lakers, Spurs, Suns, Pistons, Blazers among teams interested in Dean Wade?
item.description: Cleveland Cavaliers forward Dean Wade is expected to have various suitors in free agency, including the Cavaliers, Philadelphia 76ers, Los Angeles Lakers, San Antonio Spurs, Phoenix Suns, Detroit Pistons, and Portland Trail Blazers, league sources told HoopsHype.

item.title: Max Strus and Dennis Schroeder have been mentioned in …
item.description: Meanwhile, as the Cavaliers navigate James Harden’s return and Wade’s free agency, Cleveland’s Max Strus and Dennis Schroeder have been mentioned in trade talks with the franchise currently projected over the second apron.

item.title: Marvin Bagley expected to earn at least the taxpayer MLE
item.description: Bagley, 27, is expected to draw interest from several teams and command an average annual salary in the taxpayer mid-level exception range or slightly higher.

item.title: Saddiq Bey, Pelicans interested in an extension
item.description: Saddiq Bey is coming off the best season of his career with the New Orleans Pelicans and now both sides are interested in an extension, league sources told HoopsHype. He is eligible to sign one as early as July 11. After a torn ACL that sidelined him for the entire 2024-25 season, the 27-year-old forward averaged career highs in points (17.7) and field goal percentage (.451), while starting 64 of 72 games played. Bey was drafted in Detroit by current Pelicans executive Troy Weaver, who also trad

item.title: Landale, 30, is expected to have a strong market, …
item.description: Landale, 30, is expected to have a strong market, including interest from the Hawks, Chicago Bulls, Los Angeles Lakers, Los Angeles Clippers, Philadelphia 76ers, and Cleveland Cavaliers, league sources told HoopsHype. Expect the Australian center to command offers north of the bi-annual exception in free agency.

item.title: NBA execs: Marcus Sasser available on trade market
item.description: Furthermore, Pistons guard Marcus Sasser is said to be available on the trade market, according to NBA executives around the league who’ve spoken with HoopsHype. Sasser, a career 38.6 percent 3-point shooter, has a $5.20 million salary for the upcoming season and will then be eligible for restricted free agency the following year.

item.title: Cedric Maxwell on beef between Jaylen Brown, Stephen A. Smith: 'Why is an elephant right now battling with an ant?'
item.description: Cedric Maxwell: "But the other side of that, they gave him $300 million. If you're that mad with me and you give me $300 million, you can dangle me around like a carrot. I could care less, but in this case, I do understand that players have egos and their egos could be bruised. We've seen him go back and forth with Stephen A. Smith over and over again. I always say why is an elephant right now battling with an ant? Jaylen Brown should be beyond that."

item.title: Cedric Maxwell: "I am a huge Jaylen Brown fan. I would …
item.description: Cedric Maxwell: "I am a huge Jaylen Brown fan. I would hate to see you lose him, but I understand that there's some business aspects that come into play. If I was the Celtics right now, I'd want a hell of a package for him because Jaylen Brown was one of the top 10 players, one of the top seven players in the NBA last year. He became All-NBA, All-World essentially, and one thing he said, 'I am right now the best two-way player in the NBA other than that the alien down in San Antonio.' He has a g

item.title: Austin Reaves was going to get paid and he's got …
item.description: Law Murray: "Free agency is really difficult and these teams talk so much. That's why we have the trash rumor mill that we have now. Austin Reaves was going to get paid and he's got really good representation. These dudes have a feel and the pulse of the league and he offers an ability that, if he would have left, he would have been a difference-maker wherever he would go. I've got a lot of respect for Austin Reaves' game and so do a lot of teams in the league."

And when LeBron left Cleveland for the Lakers, Joel had one of my favorite of his troll tweets when he was like, I'm paraphrasing, but he was like, they're not going to like you in Los Angeles. That's Kobe's town. And that dude LeBron, it's been that's how it's felt. Like he's been polarizing in a Los Angeles uniform because you got Bron fans, you got Lakers fans, you got Kobe fans. But on the court he emanates confidence, barking instructions and encouragement to his teammates while shredding defenses. In the final minute of the first quarter, he drills a 3-pointer at one end before swatting one away at the other, sending a jolt of electricity through the arena. “When it comes to prospects I’ve evaluated in my 10 years, AJ is easily one of the be

When AJ was 5, his father bought a Spider-Man mini hoop, attached it to his door, and taught him to take shots from his bed. AJ was rapt. Ace later installed a 25-by-25-foot blacktop court in the backyard, and whenever someone was looking for AJ, that was the place to start. He carried his basketball everywhere and slept with it tucked under his arm. In sixth grade, AJ started working with trainer Brandon Ball, whose session

item.description: Now, we’ve heard from Mitchell Robinson himself. In an interview with WGNO (h/t New York Basketball, Robinson was asked about the possibility of returning to New York and building on the franchise’s first title in 53 years. “We can see what happens. It would be great, try to do it, try to run it back again, try to go back-to-back… Defending champs, so we’ll, that’s very a possibility.” — Mitchell Robinson. item.title: Lakers have tendered a two-way qualifying offer to …
item.description: Keith Smith: The Los Angeles Lakers have tendered a two-way qualifying offer to Chris Manon, a league source told @spotrac. Manon will now be a restricted free agent this summer.

item.title: Timberwolves have tendered a qualifying offer to …
item.description: Keith Smith: The Minnesota Timberwolves have tendered a qualifying offer to Jaylen Clark and a two-way qualifying offer to Enrique Freeman, a league source told @spotrac. Clark and Freeman will now be restricted free agents this offseason. Clark has reportedly agreed to a new deal already.

item.title: Dru Smith's $2.6 million salary for next season …
item.description: Anthony Chiang: Dru Smith's $2.6 million salary for next season becomes fully guaranteed if he's still on the Heat's roster past 11:59 p.m. today.

item.title: Karlo Matkovic: ‘The role of a veteran is very …
item.description: Karlo Matkovic: ‘The role of a veteran is very important, and DeAndre Jordan really helped me a lot this year. It helps to have a team like that where someone doesn't just come to me and say 'Cheers' and then ignore me. He learned from Jokić, he learned from Dončić. (…) He really turned out to be an 'extra' veteran. I go with him after games; he calls me, we joke around, it's great. But you can also see how he maintains his body—it’s unreal.’

item.title: Whether Bronny is a professional at that level yet is …
item.description: Karlo Matkovic on LeBron James: ‘He literally made a son to be his teammate. People talk about him and say he’s not good, but at the very least, he brought his son into the league. LeBron said he can play, he said '100% believe me.' And Bronny is not bad in the G League; he is strong, even though he is small. item.description: Vladimir Radmanovic on being traded to Hornets: ‘After being kept on the bench for nearly two months with only 'teaspoon' minutes, I couldn't establish any continuity as a player. It was one of the most frustrating periods of my career. I eventually went to Mitch Kupchak and told him, 'If this is going to continue, please count me out and look for a trade.' item.description: Vladimir Radmanovic: 'Kobe Bryant was like a shark; if he sensed even a little bit of blood, it was over. He tested every single teammate to see what he could expect from them in terms of mental toughness. This involved provocations, playing dirty during practice, and even throwing 'cheap shots.' To an outsider, it might look like something was wrong with him or that he wasn't balanced, but from the inside, you realized it was a constant test. I saw players like Smush Parker fail that test. item.description: Vladimir Radmanovic on being recruited by the Lakers: ‘When I was a free agent deciding where to sign, my manager told me that three people were going to contact me: Kobe Bryant, Magic Johnson, and Phil Jackson. No matter how humble you try to be, it is incredibly flattering when those three individuals call you personally and tell you they want you in their organization. Vlade Divac acted as a mediator, likely sharing my phone number. I knew that joining the Lakers might not be the best option

item.description: Tony Parker officially became the head coach of LDLC-ASVEL Villeurbanne last night. French Hall of Fame member will start his coaching career with the simultaneous role of being a coach and a president of the club at the same time. In an exclusive interview with L'Equipe, Parker talked in detail about his arrival to the sidelines: "This choice became logical over time. When I started the process of becoming a coach, I was more focused on the NBA. But between my attachment to my country, the fact

item.title: Nikola Jovic says Tyler Herro was in 'every single' Heat trade rumor
item.description: Nikola Jovic: ‘Ever since I arrived in Miami, I have been in trade rumors for Kevin Durant twice. Yes, twice for KD. For Kyrie Irving twice. For Damian Lillard, it was already a done deal because Lillard publicly stated that he wanted to come to Miami. It was like, 'I want Miami,' and that was it. For Lillard! And now most recently, I was in there for Giannis. I have been in seven or eight trade rumors already. Me and my brother Tyler Herro. I mean, my brother Tyler Herro, what he has endured, i

item.title: Cedric Maxwell: If I was the Celtics right now, I'd want a hell of a package for Jaylen Brown
item.description: Cedric Maxwell: I’m a huge Jaylen Brown fan. Let's start there. I would that you would lose him, but I understand that there's some business aspects that come into play. If I was the Celtics right now, I'd want a hell of a package for him because Jaylen Brown was one of the top 10 players, one of the top seven players in the NBA last year. He became All-NBA. And one thing he said, I am right now the best two-way player in the NBA other than, that the alien down in San Antonio.

item.description: Patrick Beverley: I can never disrespect Dwyane Wade, but if you ask me an honest question of who's better, I'm not just going to be on some like ignorant sh*t. Like I'mma go like, "Oh, James Harden is better." Like he's a better scorer. He's a better passer. He shoots the three better. He gets to the free throw line more. He has more triple-doubles. He has scored the more opponents. He has more MVPs. He's never missed the playoffs, more playoffs experience. And the more… I mean, Wade has a ring

item.description: Patrick Beverley when he asked out of the Clippers: ‘I text Kawhi Leonard like, "Yo, I'm just letting you know I asked for a trade, you one of my closest dudes on the team. I text Kawhi. I text Paul George. I text Marcus Morris. I'm just letting you know. I ask for, it's time for extension. Kawhi say, "I call you back." All right. I go up to my room. Never forget this. We in like I think we in the Wynn hotel, like in a meeting area. I go up to my room. Come back. My agent called me like, "Yo, co

item.title: Miles Bridges to Phoenix
item.description: Shams Charania: BREAKING: The Charlotte Hornets are trading Miles Bridges, a 2029 first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick to the Phoenix Suns for Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale and a 2033 first-round pick, sources tell ESPN.

item.title: Rockets are likely to extend a qualifying offer to …
item.description: Kelly Iko: The Houston Rockets are likely to extend a qualifying offer to wing Tari Eason, sources tell @YahooSports.

item.title: Heat targeting Tim Hardaway Jr. and Mike Conley
item.description: League sources say that the Heat will have strong interest in the veteran duo of Tim Hardaway Jr. and Mike Conley Jr.

item.title: Warriors expected to pursue Jock Landale
item.description: League sources say that the Warriors, though, are planning to register interest in various other free agents while waiting to see how James' highly anticipated free agency plays out. Sources say that Golden State is among the teams expected to pursue veteran big man Jock Landale in addition to scoring guards such as Anfernee Simons and Collin Sexton.

item.title: Spurs, Magic and Sixers interested in John Collins
item.description: League sources say John Collins certainly has fans in Minnesota, but it appears unlikely that the Timberwolves will have sufficient spending power to pursue the scoring forward, who spent last season with the Clippers. Collins is also expected to draw interest from Orlando, San Antonio and Philadelphia once free agency begins. The 76ers and Western Conference champion Spurs continue to get linked in free agency projections to the top forwards in the marketplace.

item.title: Jay Triano, who has coached both the Raptors and the …
item.description: Sources say Jay Triano, who has coached both the Raptors and the Suns in addition to numerous stops as an assistant and a lengthy stint as head coach of Canada's national team, is a leading candidate to join Micah Nori’s first coaching staff in Portland after working on Jason Kidd’s staff in Dallas last season. Nori’s first coaching job in the NBA came after working as an advance scout for more than a decade when Triano made him part of his Raptors coaching staff.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard back to Toronto?
item.description: Jake Fischer: The Raptors and Clippers have held real trade conversations this weekend on sending Kawhi Leonard back to Toronto, according to the league sources.

item.title: Toronto has expressed a preference in dealing Brandon …
item.description: Jake Fischer: In discussions with the Clippers, sources say Toronto has expressed a preference in dealing Brandon Ingram to Los Angeles, as opposed to RJ Barrett.

item.title: LeBron James has not expressed interest in returning to Heat yet
item.description: Speculation continues to swirl about whether LeBron James could have interest in a return to the Heat. Nothing should be ruled out, but this is not something that has been actively pursued by James to this point, according to a source. Miami very likely would explore if James decides to pursue it.

item.title: Heat linked to Khris Middleton
item.description: Other potential targets have not been confirmed, but Miami has been strongly linked to veteran NBA forward Khris Middleton, who played with soon-to-be-new-Heat-forward Giannis Antetekounmpo in Milwaukee.

item.title: The Heat is expected to try to add at least two …
item.description: The Heat is expected to try to add at least two skilled three-point shooters in free agency. Other options, listed here, include Landry Shamet, Anfernee Simons and Quentin Grimes, among others.

item.title: I can confirm there will be Heat interest in Tim …
item.description: Barry Jackson: With regard to the Heat report by the very hard-working @TheSteinLine and @JakeLFischer , I can confirm there will be Heat interest in Tim Hardaway Jr. when free agency begins Tuesday night, per a source. This would be a very sensible marriage if it happens... With regard to Mike Conley, he has received some consideration internally. But there are some internally who would prefer going a younger route.

item.title: During his rookie season, Cooper Flagg became the …
item.description: Crazy Stats: During his rookie season, Cooper Flagg became the youngest player in @NBA history to record games of 35, 40, 45, and 50 points, as well as the youngest player to record at least 10 assists in a game.

item.title: Nets decline option on Ziaire Williams
item.description: Michael Scotto: The Brooklyn Nets will decline their $6.25 million team option on Ziaire Williams, league sources told @hoopshype. The 24-year-old forward averaged 10.2 points in 56 games played for Brooklyn last season. Williams will become an unrestricted free agent.

item.title: Nuggets looking for another ballhandler
item.description: The Nuggets are not allowed to discuss the extension with Jokić until July 6 and, per team sources, don’t yet have clarity about how he will handle it. In the interim, front-office co-heads Jon Wallace and Ben Tenzer are focused on improving a team that fell to the Minnesota Timberwolves in the first round in late April. More specifically, league sources say, the Nuggets are on the lookout for another creative ballhandler.

item.title: However, team sources say that there has been no …
item.description: But there is a fascinating financial factor to consider, too, as Denver wants to re-sign restricted free agent forward Peyton Watson and has been widely expected to shed salary in order to make that move more feasible. Denver also wants to re-sign 25-year-old small forward Spencer Jones. However, team sources say that there has been no mandate from Nuggets ownership to cut costs. As such, it remains to be seen how aggressively — or perhaps delicately — the Nuggets move forward.

item.title: Mavs also interested in Cam Johnson
item.description: Rival teams consistently point to Nuggets forward Cam Johnson, acquired last summer in a deal that sent away Michael Porter Jr., as the most likely candidate to be dealt, in large part because the 30-year-old has just one season left on his deal at $23 million. Miami and Dallas are believed to be among the many interested teams.

item.title: To this point, however, league sources say that while …
item.description: Gordon remains a beloved member of Denver’s group. He has a two-way skill set that is coveted and rare around the league, but league sources say the Nuggets are listening to offers for the 30-year-old who has missed significant time the past two seasons with injuries. To this point, however, league sources say that while there are a lot of teams interested in acquiring Gordon, that interest remains underwhelming to the Nuggets when compared to how they value him.

item.title: For those asking about Anfernee Simons in the wake of …
item.description: Barry Jackson: For those asking about Anfernee Simons in the wake of Bobby Marks saying he would be perfect fit at the minimum for Heat, feedback I've received is that he will enter free agency looking for more than that, understandably (averaged 14.9 ppg, 38.1 on 3s in career). There are always players who fall through cracks and take minimums (like Hardaway with Denver last year, Oubre with 76ers two years ago, etc. etc.). Heat will be poised to pounce if the right player falls through the cra

item.title: “I would like to say I can be a lockdown defender. …
item.description: “I would like to say I can be a lockdown defender. Obviously, I haven’t guarded the best in the world yet, but I’m willing to take this challenge. [A] 6-10 wingspan, that can help me a bit,” Peterson said. “Just my effort. I might not be the fastest guy, or quickest guy, but my effort, I will be able to take out some of that.”

item.title: Mavs discussed a trade package with Clippers for Kawhi Leonard
item.description: Mavericks president Masai Ujiri has interest in reuniting with Kawhi Leonard, multiple league sources with knowledge of Dallas’ thinking told The Athletic. The Mavericks and LA Clippers have discussed a deal that would send the seven-time All-Star Leonard to Dallas for a package that would include P.J. Washington, Klay Thompson and draft picks, league sources said.

item.title: Warriors trying to trade for Anthony Davis to entice LeBron James to join
item.description: The Warriors are attempting to trade for Wizards big Anthony Davis and then sign Lakers free agent forward LeBron James, according to multiple league sources.

item.title: Sources say the Warriors hope adding Davis would help …
item.description: Sources say the Warriors hope adding Davis would help lure LeBron from Los Angeles to the Bay Area once free agency officially opens on June 30. The pitch would be simple: reunite with AD, team up with Steph Curry and Draymond Green, play for Steve Kerr, and chase one more championship with a roster of legends.

item.title: Ja Morant expected to be traded this week
item.description: Sources say the Heat had interest in Grizzlies point guard Ja Morant before the Giannis deal, but there is not much expectation that he will get bought out. In fact, league sources expect Morant to be traded this week.

item.title: League sources say the Heat have shopped Nikola Jović …
item.description: League sources say the Heat have shopped Nikola Jović in an attempt to cut salary to open flexibility for Powell. But Jović is entering the first year of a four-year, $62 million contract that already looks like an albatross by role player standards given his lack of development at 23 years old. Miami would have to attach draft capital to Jović’s contract to dump him, but the front office only has a 2029 first and swaps in 2028 and 2032 to dangle.

item.title: League sources say that interest on the part of the …
item.description: League sources say that interest on the part of the Mavericks and Raptors is genuine, though. It’s just a matter of what Clippers owner Steve Ballmer wants to do.

item.title: Pelicans general manager Joe Dumars has been pushing …
item.description: League sources say multiple teams have put two first-round picks on the table for Murphy. Pelicans general manager Joe Dumars has been pushing for three firsts in discussions so far, and there is still a chance he gets there. But for now, teams appear to be holding firm at two.

item.title: Hawks picking up option for Buddy Hield
item.description: Michael Scotto: The Atlanta Hawks will fully guarantee the $9.66 million salary for Buddy Hield, league sources told @hoopshype. Hield is a career 39.5 percent 3-point shooter.

item.title: Definitely hearing the Hawks are involved in several …
item.description: Jake Fischer: Definitely hearing the Hawks are involved in several trade scenarios that could end up utilizing Buddy Hield’s salary for 2026-27.

item.title: With Buddy Hield on the books at his full $9.6M …
item.description: Keith Smith: With Buddy Hield on the books at his full $9.6M salary, the Atlanta Hawks are roughly $7.1M under the luxury tax and $15.1M under the first apron. The Hawks have one open roster spot. This factors in the Aaron Wiggins trade, plus both first-round draft picks.

item.title: As far as I can tell, it's still unclear whether …
item.description: Josh Lewenberg: As far as I can tell, it's still unclear whether Clippers are really open to moving Kawhi & whether Kawhi is really open to a Toronto reunion or if they're just posturing. Those are obviously key factors, in addition to what other teams are offering (tho Kawhi market is limited)

item.title: Should also note, as I have before: in 13 years under …
item.description: Josh Lewenberg: Should also note, as I have before: in 13 years under this Masai Ujiri and now Bobby Webster-led front office, the Raptors have never moved multiple 1st-round picks in a trade. Don't expect them to do it for a 35-year-old Kawhi Leonard.

item.title: Warriors head coach Steve Kerr met with Robinson after …
item.description: Now as he enters his 11th season with the Warriors, Robinson is about to step into a new role as the team’s NBA Summer League head coach. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr met with Robinson after the season ended and told him the news, and that he thought manning the sidelines throughout summer league would be a great opportunity for Robinson's personal and professional career development as the next challenge. Naming Khalid Robinson as the Warriors’ summer league head coach falls in line with how

item.title: Jordan Clarkson could return to Knicks?
item.description: Don’t rule out a Jordan Clarkson reunion. Despite James Dolan’s mandate to stay under the second apron, Clarkson’s re-signing is “still a possibility,” a source told The Post. Clarkson, 34, will become an unrestricted free agent Tuesday after one eventful season with the Knicks, which ended with a championship but included erratic playing time.

item.title: The Raptors' interest in Kawhi was described to me as …
item.description: Josh Lewenberg: The Raptors' interest in Kawhi was described to me as "real but conditional." Contingent on price, obviously. Hard to see them paying more than last time, so think similar framework: secondary star (Ingram), former lottery pick (Dick), 1st-rounder in the following year's draft.

item.title: David West: 'The nerd influence is too much'
item.description: David West: I am neither insecure nor lack the intelligence to understand data. Im a fan of the game, a lifer if you will, but the nerd influence is too much. Style, nuance, individualism, mid range, post play, all gone. Dweeb based basketball is predictable. 3s or 2s, nothing else.

item.title: League revenue, however, will flow overwhelmingly to …
item.description: Sportico spoke recently with multiple people involved in building NBA Europe. Under the condition of anonymity, they broke down the economic structure of the league, which is planning to launch in October 2027. At the outset, league equity will be split 50/50 between the NBA and the owners of the 12 initial permanent franchises. League revenue, however, will flow overwhelmingly to the teams themselves, largely in the form of fixed distributions and performance payments, the people said.

item.title: League is committed to funding all of the NBA Europe's losses as it gets off the ground
item.description: The NBA is still finalizing how exactly to allocate the billions raised in the initial team sales, but much of it will be placed on the NBA Europe balance sheet for initial operating capital and reserves. As a result, the NBA is committed to funding all of the new league’s losses as it gets off the ground, the people said, insulating franchise owners from capital calls as the new entity tries to scale into a profitable, standalone operation. The NBA will take a cut of league revenue once there i

item.title: The current plan is to launch NBA Europe next year …
item.description: The current plan is to launch NBA Europe next year with 12 permanent franchises and four clubs that secure rotating slots via competition in other FIBA circuits. For those first dozen teams, the group is speaking with bidders in Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Istanbul, London, Lyon, Madrid, Manchester, Milan, Munich, Paris and Rome. That’s a footprint that intentionally indexes heavily on Western Europe, which has wealthier markets even if it might be further removed from the continent’s more ardent

item.title: The permanent franchise sales will produce billions in …
item.description: The permanent franchise sales will produce billions in capital, with some bids involving London and Paris already topping $1 billion, sources said. While the NBA hasn’t finalized exactly how that money will be divvied up, the majority of it will be used to fund the league’s upfront costs and early operations, the people said. That includes team distributions, reserves, marketing capital and staffing. A portion could also be distributed to existing NBA owners as a dividend of sorts.

item.title: NBA Europe franchise bids for London and Paris already topping $1 billion
item.description: NBA Europe’s central revenue will include bigger media packages, league-wide sponsorships, merchandise and licensing opportunities, and perhaps some infrastructure projects. Those revenues will be largely transferred back to the teams, essentially via a preferred distribution, the sources said. Initially, more than 80% will go to teams via a fixed payment made to all clubs (similar to the NFL’s annual distributions) and a performance pool, which will filter more money to teams based on their on-

item.description: That’s an example of league economics modeled more on traditional European soccer than the NBA or other U.S. circuits. In the first six years the league is planning more than $1.5 billion in fixed and performance distributions to its clubs, one source said. The rotating clubs will share equally in those payments, per sources. The NBA and its bankers have told prospective buyers that they expect the league to be profitable within its first decade, sources said. Once there is positive net income,

item.description: There’s also the possibility that some bidders will look to purchase existing teams as part of their push for NBA Europe inclusion. Given the fact that bid complexity (and number of bidders) will vary widely by market, the league is expecting to announce winning groups in a staggered manner as they’re finalized, the source said.

item.title: Cameron Boozer: Memphis is going to really surprise people this year

item.title: Cameron Boozer: "I don't cheat the game, I show up at …
item.description: Cameron Boozer: "I don't cheat the game, I show up at work, I have high energy and I think it starts with great coaching. I have always been surrounded by great coaches and players who really want to buy in and win. For me, I was always the best player on my team doing the right things, and it just trickles down and everyone starts doing the right things. People talk about my winning, but you can't do that without a team."

item.title: On Sunday, I went to the Liberty-Sparks game on the …
item.description: The WNBA’s biggest problem is the gulf between how good it feels to be a WNBA fan and how toxic the league seems from the outside looking in. The environment inside a WNBA arena is palpably life-affirming. The fans are more friendly than those of other sports. The players are more accessible. On Sunday, I went to the Liberty-Sparks game on the 30th anniversary of their first meeting, the inaugural game of the WNBA. I felt the gravitas and gratitude of Lisa Leslie, who played in that inaugural cl

item.title: The WNBA has changed my brain chemistry in ways I …
item.description: This week, I had a conversation on my WNBA podcast with USA Today’s Callie Fin about how the league empowered her during a medically dangerous pregnancy. The WNBA has changed my brain chemistry in ways I couldn’t have imagined. I show up to the arena less self-conscious, more authentic. I’ve had conversations about identity, community, and ambition around this league that simply do not happen in many other corners of professional sports. This is a league that’s anchored by vital fan communities

item.title: The Nuggets still have a great deal of confidence that …
item.description: While chatter will likely continue until there’s another long-term commitment from Nikola Jokic to the Denver Nuggets, team sources tell The Athletic the 31-year-old is still signaling a desire to remain in the Mile High City past his current contract. item.title: The Clippers naturally trying to extract more than has …
item.description: Dialogue between the teams continued Sunday, league sources say, with the Clippers naturally trying to extract more than has been offered if they indeed are parting with their Face of the Franchise, while the Raptors remain adamant about trying to build a deal — which also would naturally include a level of draft capital — around scoring forward Brandon Ingram and Gradey Dick rather than Canadian-born swingman RJ Barrett.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard trying to strong-arm his way out of Clippers?

item.title: Said another: “The Clippers are willing to move him … …
item.description: Said another: “The Clippers are willing to move him … and I think a lot of teams are wary of acquiring Kawhi because you just don't know if he's going to play … there’s risk there, obviously. Toronto had him, and so maybe feels more comfortable that he would play for them, could play for them.”

item.description: We're also hearing that the Clippers might elect to try to re-sign forward John Collins, who as The Stein Line previously reported is expected to draw interest from the likes of San Antonio, Orlando and Philadelphia once free agency formally begins Tuesday night at 6 PM ET.

item.title: Suns to extend Miles Bridged contract eventually

The plan is that Bridges will not just be here for one year - at some point not sure when they would like to extend him. To replace Grayson Allen the Suns are looking at 7 to 8 free agent shooting guards. So, another move coming here in free agency soon.

item.title: Sources are telling me that he’s expected to attract …
item.description: The chatter is building momentum as the NBA heads into the opening of its free agency period on Tuesday night. The Raptors have some business to focus on there, too, with power forward Sandro Mamukelashvili expected to opt out of the final year of his $2.8-million deal on Monday. Sources are telling me that he’s expected to attract multiple offers starting at more than $10 million a year, which could make it challenging for the Raptors to keep him.

item.title: Clippers interested in Goga Bitadze
item.description: Word is that the Clippers are also among the teams that have expressed trade interest in Orlando's Goga Bitadze. The Stein Line has since learned, though, that the Magic have rebuffed inquires for the Georgian big man to this point. It appears that Orlando wants to retain Bitadze in part because it is bracing for the loss of Moritz Wagner, brother of Magic star Franz Wagner, in unrestricted free agency.

item.title: Lakers eyeing Ziaire Williams
item.description: According to a league source, one player the Lakers could take a look at in free agency is Brooklyn small forward Zaire Williams, who had his team option declined by the Nets on Sunday. The Lakers have desires to get younger and more athletic on the wing, and Williams is coming off back-to-back seasons in Brooklyn where he averaged more than 10 points and shot better than 34 percent from 3-point range.

item.title: Brooklyn declining Ziaire Williams' $6.25 million team …
item.description: Brooklyn declining Ziaire Williams' $6.25 million team option, as reported by HoopsHype and the New York Post, could be a prelude to the Nets re-signing him to a longer deal using their room exception once they're done using all their cap space. For now, the Nets have $36 million in functional cap room.

item.title: Team sources say that there has been no mandate from …
item.description: Denver wants to re-sign restricted free agent forward Peyton Watson and has been widely expected to shed salary in order to make that move more feasible. Denver also wants to re-sign 25-year-old small forward Spencer Jones. However, team sources say that there has been no mandate from Nuggets ownership to cut costs. As such, it remains to be seen how aggressively — or perhaps delicately — the Nuggets move forward.

item.description: The Heat will guarantee Smith’s full $2.6 million salary for next season, according to a league source. Miami had a Sunday deadline of 11:59 p.m. to waive Smith and shed his $2.6 million salary cap hit for this upcoming season.

item.title: The Las Vegas Diamond Arena, one of the proposed sites …
item.description: The Las Vegas Diamond Arena, one of the proposed sites for a possible NBA franchise, announced Monday that it has purchased the last piece of land needed for the project. According to a release, the Diamond Arena has completed the purchase of an additional 3.03 acres, giving the project full control of its development site at the northeast corner of Las Vegas Boulevard and Four Seasons Drive, directly across from Mandalay Bay.

item.title: The completed purchase cements the project’s position …
item.description: The completed purchase cements the project’s position as a fully entitled and development-ready site. The proposed arena features 21,212 seats and is designed for NBA basketball, concerts, conventions, and major events. “By closing escrow on the final parcel, we now own the entire arena site and have solidified our position as the premier venue for a future NBA franchise in Las Vegas,” said Tom Letizia, spokesman for the Diamond Arena.

item.title: A memorial service was held Monday morning for Chicago …
item.description: A memorial service was held Monday morning for Chicago Bulls broadcaster and three-time NBA champion Stacey King. The service was held at the Advocate Center, a training facility close to the United Center.

item.description: Sam Amick on Jaylen Brown: "This one is, if I had to handicap it, it just feels like somebody has got to put enough on the table to get this thing done, but Boston is asking for the sun and the moon. I keep looking at Portland and because people keep bringing Portland up when I talk to them, they wanted to go big on Giannis Antetokounmpo and that did not work. Even without a commitment, they were willing to try to do a Giannis trade. And when you see that kind of boldness, then you kind of go, a

item.title: Gov. Jenniffer González Colón welcomed NBA champion …
item.description: Gov. Jenniffer González Colón welcomed NBA champion José Alvarado of the New York Knicks on Saturday, joined by Puerto Rico Basketball Federation President Yum Ramos and Puerto Rico National Basketball Team General Manager Carlos Arroyo. Alvarado arrived on the island Thursday with his family and the NBA championship trophy.

item.title: José Alvarado is the third Puerto Rican to win an NBA …

José Alvarado is the third Puerto Rican to win an NBA championship, a feat made possible through his unique tenacity,” the governor said as she presented him with the Governor’s Medal and a proclamation.

item.title: 2026 First-round pick Bennett Stirtz: 'I thought I was going to be Division II my whole career'
item.description: During the pre-NBA Draft process, Bennett Stirtz worked out with the Chicago Bulls, Oklahoma City Thunder, Golden State Warriors, Memphis Grizzlies, Toronto Raptors and others. Now he’s in New York, getting ready for his name to be called at the 2026 NBA Draft. A few years ago, not even Stirtz thought this was possible. “Not at all,” Stirtz said. “I thought I was going to be Division II my whole career.”

item.title: Stirtz’s story might be worth a film of its own one …
item.description: Stirtz’s story might be worth a film of its own one day. In fact, a mini documentary is being made about his NBA Draft experience. But if an actual movie were to be produced, Stirtz picks Matthew McConaughey as the actor to play him. As for Ben McCollum, the energetic 45-year-old head coach, Stirtz takes a little while longer to choose who would be best for the role. “Timothée Chalamet,” Stirtz says with a smile.

item.title: Bennett Stirtz grabs a Grizzlies hat as he walks onto …
item.description: Bennett Stirtz grabs a Grizzlies hat as he walks onto the stage to shake Silver’s hand and pose for a photo. But there’s a twist. Stirtz was alerted shortly before the pick that the Grizzlies would be trading him to his actual landing spot, the Oklahoma City Thunder. “My agent — it was probably like a minute before Memphis picked — he's like, ‘You're going to OKC,’” Stirtz said. “Before anyone else knew, I knew.” McCollum called Stirtz and the Thunder a “perfect fit.”

He wondered whether there was a corresponding deal the Blazers were working on to clear up the position.

item.title: The Grizzlies saved a $13 million check to Morant by …
item.description: Regarding the Ja Morant trade, there is one important reason to do the deal now rather than in July. That is because Morant is still in year seven of his career rather than year eight, which means his max is capped at 25 percent of the cap (for a player who has completed six full years of service) rather than 30 percent. item.description: Five weeks ago I sat across from Dundon in North Carolina and he told me that he had watched “Untold: Jail Blazers,” the Netflix documentary on the era that has defined modern Trail Blazers history on a flight from Dallas to Raleigh. What he saw, he said, disgusted him. Not the flagrant and unapologetic drug use, the rape allegation or the bad attitudes, but the way fans turned on their team. His takeaway: The players didn’t do anything. Indeed, they were not caught on film waving around a handg

item.title: “Hopefully,” Dundon told me, “we’ll create a product …
item.description: When I had that conversation with Dundon in Raleigh, he said that he felt fans of the Portland teams of the early 2000s were too quick to latch onto negativity toward Blazers players. Damon’s weed. Rasheed’s tantrums. Bonzi’s birdie finger. Fans resented it all. “Hopefully,” Dundon told me, “we’ll create a product where that’s not a choice.” Indeed, there should be no choice at all for Blazers fans. The only option is unrestrained fury.

item.description: LaVine has been the subject of trade rumors and speculation for the past year, but there hasn’t been much of a market for his services due to the size of his contract. The Kings will continue to explore trade possibilities for LaVine as general manager Scott Perry works to overhaul an aging and expensive roster. If they can’t find a deal before the February trade deadline, LaVine’s expiring contract will come off the books next summer, giving Sacramento significant salary cap relief.

item.title: That is because Morant is still in year seven of his …
item.description: Regarding the Ja Morant deal, there is one important reason to do the deal now rather than in July. That is because Morant is still in year seven of his career rather than year eight, which means his max is capped at 25 percent of the max (for a player who has completed six full years of service) rather than 30 percent.

item.title: Cason Wallace open to leaving OKC?
item.description: There is a belief around the league that Wallace is open to leaving OKC, and he’s up for a big extension the Thunder might be loath to pay. The young guard would cost multiple first-round picks but be the point-of-attack defender the Nets need.

item.title: The Nets are more likely to use the space in trades …
item.description: With their tanking hopefully behind them, Brooklyn will at least try to compete this season. League sources told The Post that the Nets are more likely to use the space in trades than chasing free agents, and cap experts Bobby Marks of ESPN and Yossi Gozlan of The Third Apron agreed that’s where the value is. item.title: Wizards interested in bringing back Russell Westbrook?
item.description: League sources tell The Stein Line that Washington has a level interest in Russell Westbrook. The nine-time former All-Star's final season of the four in his career in which he averaged a triple-double (22.2 PPG, 11.5 RPG and 11.7 APG) came in 2020-21 with the Wizards.

He actually believes, however, that Morant can make a comeback to his old form because of how the guard competes when he’s healthy.

item.title: Warriors unlikely to move Jimmy Butler?
item.description: Behind the scenes, however, Golden State continues to signal a reluctance to use Butler's contract when he's injured for a move like that. Consider the strong relationships with Butler held by Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy and coach Steve Kerr. Butler and Kerr are frequently in San Diego in the offseason and known to cross paths.

item.title: Kings, Lakers both in the mix for Jalen Duren
item.description: The Jalen Duren situation is getting more interesting by the day. As we first reported Friday, the third-team All-NBA big man was underwhelmed by Detroit’s offer in restricted free agency and almost immediately began strategizing about sign-and-trade scenarios out of town. And as we learned Monday afternoon via league sources, the Sacramento Kings and Los Angeles Lakers are now officially on that list.

item.title: The Kings and Lakers are scheduled to meet with Duren …
item.description: Those sources, who are not authorized to discuss free-agent scenarios before the offseason officially begins, say the Kings and Lakers are scheduled to meet with Duren after free agency opens Tuesday. It’s unclear whether the Kings’ visit will be in person or virtual, but those sources say the Lakers’ meeting is expected to be by phone.

item.title: Luka Doncic a big fan of Jalen Duren's game
item.description: (The Lakers’ incumbent starting center, Deandre Ayton, picked up his $8.1 million player option Monday.) Yet in stark contrast to the Kings’ scenario, the Lakers’ best offerings might be draft capital rather than quality players, as Detroit could trade Duren into the Lakers’ salary-cap space. Lakers star Luka Dončić is known to be a fan of Duren’s game, league sources say, which is a monumental factor for any player who’s trying to be welcomed into Crypto.com Arena these days.

item.title: Luka Doncic for his desire to pair with an "A-list …

One of the teams is the Los Angeles Lakers, a source familiar with the situation told ESPN. L.A.'s front office has been given feedback from franchise star Luka Doncic for his desire to pair with an "A-list center," a league source told ESPN, and Duren would certainly fit the bill. item.title: The Blazers now have four point guards — Morant, …
item.description: That leads to the unspoken part of this trade: more deals are on the way. Have to be. The Blazers now have four point guards — Morant, Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Henderson — so unloading one or two seems likely. If I was to guess, I would imagine Holiday, because of his contract and because of his skill set, is the more likely candidate to be traded next.

item.title: They want more big-man depth and realize they have a …
item.description: The Blazers are still in the market to make another deal. They want more big-man depth and realize they have a logjam of four point guards with Morant, Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson, but the team does not feel it is essential to unload one of its guards. The Blazers believe the four guards can co-exist, in large part because the team believes Holiday can alleviate the redundancy by playing him off the ball as a shooting guard or small forward.

item.title: Donovan Clingan off limits in trade talks
item.description: One thing has become certain about the Trail Blazers after Monday’s trade for point guard Ja Morant: Portland center Donovan Clingan is now essentially off limits in trade talks, according to a team source.

item.title: The Kings are not expected to pursue free agent …
item.description: On a related note, the Kings are not expected to pursue free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga, according to league sources who were granted anonymity to discuss free-agent scenarios before Tuesday. The Atlanta Hawks declined Kuminga’s team option Monday, making the 23-year-old an unrestricted free agent. The Kings attempted to acquire Kuminga last offseason via a sign-and-trade scenario but could not agree to a deal with Kuminga’s former team, the Golden State Warriors.

item.title: Lakers eyeing Sandro Mamukelashvili
item.description: But people around the NBA, tasked with trying to make sense of the evolving free-agency landscape, started to link the Lakers to a wide range of players throughout Monday. One name has come up from multiple league sources: Toronto forward/center Sandro Mamukelashvili. Mamukelashvili declined his $2.8 million option with the Raptors Monday, with league sources believing he could command $10 million or more in free agency.

item.title: #Cavs and Dean Wade are having ongoing negotiations …
item.description: Chris Fedor: On the eve of NBA free agency, sources tell @clevelanddotcom that #Cavs and Dean Wade are having ongoing negotiations and dialogue. Both sides plan to keep working to see if a deal is possible before free agency Tuesday. Neither side has closed the door on a return to Cleveland.

item.title: The Blazers have interest in retaining all three …
item.description: The Blazers’ 15-man regular season roster features 10 players under guaranteed contract and two more — Vit Krejčí and Sidy Cissoko — with team options. The Blazers are expected to exercise both team options, giving them 12 players under contract. This leaves them with three unrestricted free agents: Robert Williams III, Matisse Thybulle and Blake Wesley. item.title: They are not expected to retain free agent center …
item.description: The Blazers have immediate needs at center and power forward. They are not expected to retain free agent center Robert Williams III, who is hoping to land a contract in the $15 million a year range, leaving only second-year center Yang Hansen as a backup to Donovan Clingan. The Blazers are also thin at power forward, with Deni Avdija and Toumani Camara their only options.

item.title: Josh Okogie is among a group of swingmen they are …
item.description: Sources say Josh Okogie is among a group of swingmen they are looking at to support the soon-to-be-back-from-injury Tyrese Haliburton. Indiana can pay part of the non-taxpayer midlevel to compete against other teams' prospective offers at the veteran's minimum and is also said to have Gary Trent Jr. and Kelly Oubre Jr. on its list.

item.title: The Washington Wizards decline their team option for …
item.description: Keith Smith: The Washington Wizards decline their team option for Jamir Watkins, a league source told @spotrac . The Wizards did tender a qualifying offer to Watkins. He'll now be a restricted free agent this offseason.

Right now, I'm taking the Anthony Davis thing off the front burner. I do not have data that says that that's likely to happen.

item.title: Rockets expected to land Marcus Smart

item.title: Suns have a strong level of interest in Luke Kennard

item.title: After eight seasons with the Lakers, including leading …
item.description: Shams Charania: After eight seasons with the Lakers, including leading the franchise to the 2020 NBA championship, James departs and enters free agency set to join a new team. Lakers president Rob Pelinka and Rich Paul spoke a short time ago about the four-time champion's plans, sources said. James chose to inform the Lakers well before start of free agency tonight out of courtesy and appreciation for their run together, and to allow LA to conduct its offseason business.

item.title: LeBron James has informed the Lakers he is leaving and …
item.description: Dan Woike: LeBron James has informed the Lakers he is leaving and will be playing elsewhere next season, sources close to James say. He has not yet decided where he’ll be playing next season and felt it was time to move on.

item.title: Overall Giannis getting to go to one of the places he …
item.description: Draymond Green: As it stands today, I don’t think it leaves Giannis in a much better position next year than he would’ve been with the Bucks. However, the long run I think definitely leaves them in a better position because you can build that team out. We saw even when LeBron and Chris Bosh went to the Miami Heat, that team looked a bit different the second year than the first year. Overall Giannis getting to go to one of the places he preferred to go to, I think it’s great.

item.title: Jalen Brunson says when he signed in New York, he …
item.description: Legion Hoops: Jalen Brunson says when he signed in New York, he always wanted to wear No. 13 to honor his favorite player, Steve Nash, but he wasn’t able to get it from Evan Fournier.

item.title: Warriors 'at the front of the line' in pursuit of LeBron James
item.description: Marc Stein: The Warriors are at the front of the line in pursuit of LeBron James in free agency and league sources tell @TheSteinLine that Golden State is not operating as though it has a mandate to also pursue an Anthony Davis trade.

item.title: Cavaliers have interest in second reunion with LeBron James
item.description: Chris Haynes: Cleveland Cavaliers have interest in a second reunion with LeBron James with the appeal of the franchise’s greatest player finishing his career where it all started, league sources tell me.

item.title: There was nothing percolating on LeBron front for …
item.description: Barry Jackson: There was nothing percolating on LeBron front for Miami when the Heat opted not to create full mid-level money in recent days. They could create full $15.1 mid-level money, if LeBron somewhat surprisingly decides to leave the West and come here, by attaching a draft pick to Jovic with hope of finding a taker.

item.title: Jock Landale to return to Hawks
item.description: Shams Charania: Free agent center Jock Landale intends to sign a one-year, $14 million deal to return to the Atlanta Hawks, sources tell ESPN. Landale had a strong finish after being traded to the Hawks, averaging 10.6 points and 5.7 rebounds last season, and his agents Sammy Wloszczowski and Mike Lelchitski of SIG Sports finalized the deal Tuesday.

item.title: "I definitely think it's something to keep an eye on, …
item.description: ESPN Cleveland: "I definitely think it's something to keep an eye on, that's one to keep an eye on," - @WindhorstESPN on the Cavs potentially trading Max Strus.

item.description: ESPN Cleveland: "They are working on trades, I'm not going to tell you who they're working on because I can't deal with it in my life," - @WindhorstESPN on the Cavs right now 🤣🤣🤣

item.title: LeBron James to Warriors not a done deal yet
item.description: Anthony Slater: Warriors decision makers have been given no indication at this hour that they are the firm LeBron James landing spot, per sources. There's a belief that they'll have plenty of appeal, but appears to be some level of recruitment required.

item.title: Golden State will certainly be pitching LeBron James …
item.description: Jake Fischer: Golden State will certainly be pitching LeBron James to join Stephen Curry and Draymond Green with the Warriors. From last night: "Golden State is known to be the league's most interested external suitor for the 41-year-old."

item.title: LeBron James to Miami has been discussed around the league as a possibility
item.description: Heat Central: REPORT: LeBron James has been linked to the Miami Heat after the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade, per @JakeLFischer “He’s been connected to Miami, a potential homecoming there once Giannis was traded to South Beach. There’s plenty talk around the league that they could see that reunion”

item.title: The Hawks will use nearly their entire $15 million …
item.description: Yossi Gozlan: The Hawks will use nearly their entire $15 million mid-level exception to sign Jock Landale to this contract. His Non Bird rights are too low for him to receive this without the MLE. Going rate for premium reserve big men is $14 million annually between him and Robert Williams.

item.description: SportsCenter: I'm told this is a happiness-led decision for LeBron James. ... Wherever he lands in free agency, it will not be driven by money." But there's no question all of the NBA's contending teams are in the picture for LeBron James. Rich Paul will call LeBron with expressed interest as soon as free agency opens up tonight. item.description: Heat Central: “You look at teams he’s been too, you look at the Cavs, and you look at the Heat. He’s been in those places. He knows the terrain. I think it’s too soon to say anyone is the front runner” — @TheSteinLine on LeBron destinations

item.title: LeBron James, Luka Doncic had no personal issues with each other; James departure unrelated to Doncic
item.description: There might be an instinct here to think that Luka Doncic helped push LeBron James out the door, but league sources who know both, who were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss the situation, insist the two players had no personal issues with one another. James, after all, went to the Lakers, and said Dončić should have his name introduced last in the starting lineups. And this summer, LeBron and Luka shared text messages about golf, a hobby they've both picked up in t

item.title: Jock Landale’s new one-year, $14 million deal to …
item.description: Kelly Iko: Jock Landale’s new one-year, $14 million deal to return to Atlanta is fully guaranteed, sources tell @YahooSports .

item.title: Celtics unlikely to trade Jaylen Brown under current asking price
item.description: A quick word on Jaylen Brown, as his sticky situation continues to loom so large over this offseason. Barring a drastic and unforeseen change in the market, the Boston Celtics will have to significantly lower their asking price if they plan on trading him anytime soon.

item.title: League sources have been tying the Blazers to Brown …
item.description: League sources have been tying the Blazers to Brown for some time now, but all indications are that their interest is moderate, at best. And, again, nothing close to what the Celtics have been asking for, according to sources who spoke on condition of anonymity to describe ongoing deliberations.

item.title: While the Nuggets have certainly considered the Brown …
item.description: While the Nuggets have certainly considered the Brown option, they haven’t spoken to the Celtics since the weekend and their interest has been significantly overstated, according to team sources who spoke on condition of anonymity to describe ongoing negotiations. There’s a familiar obstacle, too, as the Nuggets simply don’t have the draft assets to satisfy the Celtics’ ask.

item.title: NBA Europe franchise bids coming in at at least $500 million
item.description: The latest bids for NBA Europe franchises were due Monday, and they came in at $500 million or higher in each of the 12 target cities, with multiple bids of more than $1 billion. Bids were made by more than 20 existing basketball and soccer clubs, including current EuroLeague teams, according to someone familiar with the details.

item.title: “We’re extremely encouraged by the final bids we …
item.description: For those first dozen teams, the group is speaking with bidders in Athens, Greece; Barcelona, Spain; Berlin; Istanbul; London; Lyon, France; Madrid, Spain; Manchester, England; Milan; Munich; Paris; and Rome. “We’re extremely encouraged by the final bids we received for permanent franchises,” Mark Tatum, NBA deputy commissioner, said in a statement. “This will be the biggest influx of capital European basketball has ever seen, and we have clear front-runners in each of our 12 target cities, incl

item.title: Cavaliers open to the idea of a LeBron James return
item.description: Sources tell cleveland.com that the Cavs are open to the idea of a LeBron James return. Of course, signing the franchise legend for one final stint isn’t exactly straightforward given their salary cap situation. Although cap-strapped Cleveland is currently $29.1 million below the first apron and $42.1 million below the second apron, those numbers don’t reflect the expected multiyear deal James Harden is expected to sign in the near future.

item.title: Max Strus, Dennis Schroeder on the move?
item.description: Since Cleveland’s season ended in a Game 4 loss to the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference finals, sources say the team has had discussions about the possibility of trading Max Strus and Dennis Schroder. Strus is set to make $16.6 million in the final year of his contract. Schroder is still owed nearly $31 million over the next two seasons. Those moves would help Cleveland’s salary cap situation. If the Cavs get below the punitive aprons, they could also theoretically orchestrate a sign-an

item.title: Moritz Wagner on Nets' radar
item.description: They were reportedly interested in Mitchell Robinson but the Nets also are expected to show strong interest in Orlando’s Mo Wagner in free agency, per sources. Brooklyn obviously wouldn’t sign both Robinson and Wagner.

item.title: The Knicks plan entering free agency for second-round …
item.description: The Knicks plan entering free agency for second-round pick Jack Kayil is that he play next season overseas with his current club in Germany

item.title: Celtics planning to build a new arena in Boston?
item.description: The C’s have another decade on their lease at TD Garden, so Bill Chisholm has some time to decide. But not THAT much, given how long these projects typically take. And whispers are already out there. “They’ve been looking for a long time in Boston,” one political insider said. “Financially, it’s not working for them not to have their own stadium.” The latest rumored location? Outside South Station, on land currently occupied by the US Postal Service annex along Fort Point Channel.

item.title: Other sites beyond South Station are in the air as …
item.description: Other sites beyond South Station are in the air as well. One is the former Boston Flower Exchange in the South End, where The Abbey Group has approvals to develop four buildings. That property, however, is about a mile from four T stations, which might be tough on game days.

item.title: Heat summer roster does not include Keshad Johnson, …
item.description: Ira Winderman: Heat summer roster does not include Keshad Johnson, but does include Myron Gardner, Vlad Goldin, Jahmir Young and Trevor Keels. Of that group, only Gardner presently under contract to Heat. Former Pacer and Net Kendall Brown also on Heat summer roster.

item.title: Coach Corliss Williamson says Jayden Quaintance will …
item.description: Matthew Tynan: Update from Summer Spurs practice: Coach Corliss Williamson says Jayden Quaintance will be traveling with the team throughout Summer League but will not play. Carter Bryant will be playing, but only in Las Vegas.

item.title: Luka Doncic says goodbye to LeBron James: 'An honor to play with and learn from you'
item.description: Law Murray: From Luka Doncic to LeBron James

item.title: Magic Johnson: I want to thank LeBron James and his …
item.description: Magic Johnson: I want to thank LeBron James and his super agent Rich Paul for taking a meeting with me back in 2018 when I was President of the Lakers and deciding to sign with us. He created a whole new era for the Lakers, including leading us to an NBA Championship in 2020 and all the milestones he surpassed in a Lakers jersey. I’ll always love and be grateful for him and wish him all the best in the next phase of his life, on and off the court!

item.title: OG Anunoby's game-winning ball from Finals Game 4 returned to the Knicks, won't be up for auction
item.description: The ball that New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby tipped in to seal the biggest comeback in NBA Finals history and win Game 4 against the San Antonio Spurs was returned to the Knicks shortly before it was scheduled to hit the Sotheby’s auction block Tuesday.

item.title: “The game ball from Game 4 of the 2026 NBA Finals …
item.description: “The game ball from Game 4 of the 2026 NBA Finals holds significant importance to the New York Knicks, their fans, and the city, and will remain with the team as a lasting piece of franchise history. As such, it will not be included in Sotheby’s June 30 auction, which will continue to feature a curated selection of authentic jerseys and memorabilia from the series,” an NBA spokesperson said in a statement to The Athletic when asked why the ball was withdrawn.

item.title: In the absence of the ball, perhaps the standout piece …
item.description: In the absence of the ball, perhaps the standout piece in the auction is Finals MVP Jalen Brunson’s jersey from Game 1, in which he scored 30 points, including 13 in the fourth quarter to help the Knicks jump out to an early series lead. There were 40 bids on the Brunson jersey within the first hour of the auction opening, with a high bid of $110,000.

item.title: Tim Legler says the NBA has never once pushed back on …
item.description: Tim Legler says the NBA has never once pushed back on him for criticizing officiating during a broadcast. Legler was a guest on last week’s edition of the Awful Announcing Podcast and was asked directly whether he’s ever heard from the league after criticizing an official or a call. “No, not once,” he told host Brandon Contes. “They allowed us to have these conversations.”

item.title: “We’re respectful of the process. We’re respectful of …
item.description: “We’re respectful of the process. We’re respectful of the officials,” Legler said. “So at times, yeah, you’re going to comment on a no-call or the physicality overall in a game… I think we addressed it in a respectful way, and we’re on there to do that — but to respect the game, respect the participants — and we both feel that way. I think we were able to pull that off.”

item.title: The LA Clippers will be guaranteeing Kris Dunn’s …
item.description: Law Murray: As expected, the LA Clippers will be guaranteeing Kris Dunn’s contract for the 2026-27 NBA season

item.title: LeBron James to talk to several teams after free agency opens
item.description: Ramona Shelburne: LeBron James and/or his representatives will talk to a few teams after free agency opens in a few hours. A source close to the process says there's “no rush" for him to make a decision.

item.description: LeBron James: No, THANK YOU! Truly a honor to wear the 💜💛 while trying to continuing the greatness & legacies that came before me! Hope I made a few proud during my stint. 🙏🏾🫡👑
