item.description: Shams Charania: BREAKING: The Los Angeles Clippers are nearing deal sending Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, 2 first-round picks, 1 pick swap and 2 second-rounders, sources tell ESPN. A return to Canada for the Raptors champion and two-time Finals MVP.

item.title: Lakers interested in Quentin Grimes
item.description: Marc Stein: Last night we reported the Lakers' rising interest in Toronto free agent Sandro Mamukelashvili. Now league sources tell @JakeLFischer and me that Philadelphia's Quentin Grimes is emerging as another top Lakers target. MORE Intel here: tinyurl.com/bde3f33k

item.title: Precious Achiuwa returns to Sacramento on a two-year deal
item.description: Chris Haynes: Free agent forward Precious Achiuwa has agreed on terms to re-sign with the Sacramento Kings on a two-year, $11.5M deal, league sources tell me.

item.title: Brandon Ingram and Gradey Dick plus picks for Kawhi …
item.description: Michael Grange: Not saying this is not going to happen, but per league sources, Brandon Ingram and Gradey Dick plus picks for Kawhi Leonard is not yet completed. Some details still TBD.

item.title: The Raptors luxury tax/apron situation is fluid due to …
item.description: Yossi Gozlan: The Raptors luxury tax/apron situation is fluid due to Kawhi Leonard's $7.45 million trade bonus. He will need to waive most of it unless Raptors shed more payroll. They'd have enough room to fill their final four roster spots with minimum salaries if he waives it all.

item.title: Wizards shut down trade talks for Anthony Davis
item.description: Marc J. Spears: The Washington Wizards are not interested in trading 10-time NBA All-Star forward Anthony Davis and are not listening to trade offers for him, a source told @espn @andscape. Another NBA team exec says Wizards GM Will Dawkins is a huge fan of AD.

item.title: @clevelanddotcom that Cleveland has remained engaged …
item.description: Chris Fedor: Despite the LeBron James news and #Cavs being interested, sources tell @clevelanddotcom that Cleveland has remained engaged in conversations with free agent Dean Wade about the possibility of him returning.

item.title: Leonard has the 2026-27 season left on his contract at …
item.description: Leonard has the 2026-27 season left on his contract at $50.3 million. He had preferred to stay with the Clippers, but the franchise made no long-term commitments to him this offseason, sources said.

item.title: Familiarity with a Toronto organization that has the …
item.description: Three key reasons Leonard was open to this deal to Toronto, according to sources: Familiarity with a Toronto organization that has the majority of its front office structure in place, now led by executive vice president Bobby Webster. Leonard also likes the city of Toronto and believes the Raptors can contend in the Eastern Conference.

item.title: LeBron James wants Rich Paul to talk to any team interested in signing him
item.description: Dave McMenamin: LeBron James has instructed Rich Paul to talk to everyone around the league who is interested in him playing for them and come back to him with what the options are so he can make his decision, a source familiar with James' thinking told ESPN.

item.title: After taking time to decompress and undergo some …
item.description: Dave McMenamin: After taking time to decompress and undergo some self-assessment, LeBron James came to the conclusion that he wanted to continue playing “meaningful, competitive basketball,” a source familiar with James’ thinking told ESPN.

item.title: While James is committed to returning for a 24th …
item.description: Dave McMenamin: While James is committed to returning for a 24th season, he has not made any decision as to whether that will be his final season in the NBA, the source said.

item.title: James Harden holding off on signing new deal with Cavs to see if they can get LeBron James
item.description: On Monday, Harden declined his $42.3 million player option and is now a free agent. He is expected to return to Cleveland on a new contract, but Harden is waiting to sign to give the Cavs the flexibility they need to make a move like adding LeBron for next season, according to a league source who spoke on condition of anonymity to describe ongoing deliberations.

item.title: Cavs looking to move Max Strus
item.description: To that end, the Cavs are trying to trade forward Max Strus, league sources told The Athletic, so they could sign LeBron — or perhaps another player — into that midlevel exception. Strus is slated to make $16.6 million next season. If Harden signs for $30 million, and if Cleveland can deal Strus and take back no salary in return, it would be able to give James the midlevel exception.

item.title: Because of where Toronto is with regard to the first …
item.description: Bobby Marks: Because of where Toronto is with regard to the first apron, the Kawhi Leonard proposed trade will need to wait until July 6. Leonard also has a 15% trade bonus of his remaining salary. The bonus is valued at $7.5M and the Clippers are responsible to pay. He can amend the bonus down or eliminate.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard will work with Raptors to sign two-year extension
item.description: Chris Haynes: Kawhi Leonard and Toronto Raptors will soon engage to structure out the terms on a two-year extension to lock up the future Hall of Famer through the 2028-29 season, sources say.

item.title: Leonard's and Ingram's could take a minute
item.description: Michael Grange: Given the histories of the primary players involved, it's not surprising that the last hurdle to get a deal done is each team signing off on the medicals of the incoming player, per league source. Gradey Dick? Shouldn't be a problem. Leonard's and Ingram's could take a minute.

item.title: The Clippers have 9 first-round picks now, but that …
item.description: Yossi Gozlan: Now we await the results of the Aspiration investigation. The Clippers have 9 first-round picks now, but that amount could be reduced if penalized. Between this and the Zubac trade, it makes sense to load up on first-round picks just in case.

item.description: Yossi Gozlan: The Lakers could potentially sign both Sandro Mamukelashvili & Quentin Grimes while preserving a $41.25 million max slot. One could go into their surplus cap space (~$11 million, could create more via trade). The other could go into the $9.4 million room mid-level.

item.description: Mike Vorkunov: NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the NBA has landed on clear frontrunners in 12 cities for NBA Europe after it received final bids for the league's launch. item.title: Pistons plan to match any potential offer sheet Jalen Duren signs
item.description: Marc J. Spears: The Detroit Pistons have offered what the franchise believes is the most lucrative contract possible for their All-Star restricted free agent Jalen Duren, are not interested in any sign and trade deals and will match any potential offer sheet he signs, sources @espn @andscape .

item.title: National Basketball Association announced today that …
item.description: NBA Communications: The National Basketball Association announced today that the Salary Cap for the 2026-27 season has been set at $164.961 million. The Tax Level for the 2026-27 season is $200.428 million.

item.title: The 3 teams I mentioned (Heat, GSW, CLE) you can …
item.description: Heat Central: LeBron James main priority is going to a team that has a chance at winning, per @ChrisBHaynes "I'm told he's going to be open minded and patient for his next team.... The one component a team is going to have to have to secure his service from what i'm told, is the team has to be competitive and have a realistic chance at winning.... The 3 teams I mentioned (Heat, GSW, CLE) you can pretty much look and see of those 3 who has the best shot at winning... Money wasn't mentioned"

item.title: Timberwolves have interest in LeBron James?
item.description: Cleveland and Miami are often cited as realistic landing spots as well, and the Minnesota Timberwolves are known to have interest if he felt like shocking the basketball world with that sort of move.

item.title: The Warriors are now signaling that Davis isn't in …
item.description: The Warriors are now signaling that Davis isn't in their plans, according to league sources who spoke on condition of anonymity to describe ongoing deliberations. Conversely, the Washington Wizards, the club that employs Davis, is very against the prospect of trading him to the Warriors (or, for now, anywhere), those sources said.

item.title: Being told that barring a last minute change here, …
item.description: Jake Fischer: Being told that barring a last minute change here, Dean Wade will test the market in unrestricted free agency at 6 p.m ET, where Wade is expected to field interest from several playoff teams.

item.title: Bones Hyland returning to Minnesota
item.description: Jon Krawczynski: Bones Hyland has agreed to return to the Minnesota Timberwolves next season, sources told @TheAthletic. Hyland established himself as a rotation player, teaming with Ayo Dosunmu in the "Twin Turbos" backcourt.

item.title: DeAndre Jordan re-signs with Pelicans
item.description: Chris Haynes: Free agent center DeAndre Jordan is re-signing with the New Orleans Pelicans for what will be his 19th NBA season, league sources tell me.

item.title: Ousmane Dieng signs three-year deal with Bucks
item.description: Free agent forward Ousmane Dieng has agreed to a three-year, $17.5 million deal to return to the Milwaukee Bucks, sources tell ESPN. Dieng had a strong finish to last season after his trade from OKC, and now Bucks officials finalize the deal with agents Michael Tellem of Excel Sports Management and Marius Rutkauskas.

item.title: LeBron in no rush,
item.description: Barry Jackson: LeBron in no rush, per Shams. "What does happiness mean?" is the most existential question ever uttered on SportsCenter.

Those sources indicated many of the undisclosed bids exceeded the NBA’s preferred range of $500M to $1B and that ownership groups from Athens, Barcelona, Berlin, Istanbul, London, Lyon, Madrid, Manchester, Milan, Munich, Paris and Rome all are in the run

item.title: But he was born in Marrakesh, Morocco, moved to the …
item.description: It is unknown which of those markets Lasry -- who sold the Bucks in 2023 -- is pursuing. But he was born in Marrakesh, Morocco, moved to the U.S. at the age of 7 and, according to sources, is likely not the only former NBA owner to bid for a franchise. Lasry was unavailable for comment.

item.title: The sense, according to sources, is that the winning …
item.description: The NBA’s BOG is scheduled to meet in mid-July, although it is unclear whether the governors will greenlight the franchises in just a matter of two weeks. The sense, according to sources, is that the winning bids will be announced on a rolling basis -- not all at once -- and that the NBA is still trying to sort out a potential EuroLeage partnership.

item.title: For instance, in the first decade of NBA Europe, the …
item.description: Sources said that since the NBA tweaked the league’s financial model in late April, the initial bids (due in late March) have grown by more than 100%. For instance, in the first decade of NBA Europe, the NBA expects to make over $10B in distributions, will invest over $3B right away to offset potential early-stage losses and that the 12 permanent franchises will earn money by Year 3.

item.title: Quinten Post is quietly accruing interest from a few …

Post, after all, is currently only slated to be Golden State's third big man behind Porziņģis and Al Horford. item.title: The structure of Powell’s deal gives Chicago …
item.description: After extending center Collins on Tuesday, the Bulls entered Day 2 of free agency with around $23 million in salary-cap space and the room exception of $9.4 million. With Norman Powell’s deal, the Bulls are essentially left to operate with that room exception. The structure of Powell’s deal gives Chicago flexibility to pivot after this season. It also gives it the chance to potentially capitalize on Powell’s value at the trade deadline.

item.title: Paul Pierce on LeBron James potentially joining Warriors: 'It starts to turn into a spectacle'
item.description: NBA Courtside: Paul Pierce says when he thinks about LeBron James joining the Warriors he cringes a little bit: “Because like it’s just like man, come on. But you guys are two of the biggest superstars the NBA has ever had.” (Via @NFGShow)

item.title: Norman Powell, Bulls agree to a two-year, $45 million contract
item.description: Michael Scotto: Sources: The Chicago Bulls and Norman Powell have agreed to a two-year, $45 million deal. Powell is coming off his first All-Star season and is a career 40% 3-point shooter.

item.title: Relationship between Heat, LeBron James now 'strong'
item.description: The relationship between the Heat and LeBron James initially was frosty after their breakup, but is now strong. The Heat would welcome a return by James, a source has said. Even at 41, James remains a very effective player. He averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists per game while shooting 51.5% from the field and 31.7% on threes in 60 appearances for the Lakers last season.

item.title: If LeBron James wants to return to the Heat, the team …
item.description: If LeBron James wants to return to the Heat, the team would have interest in making that happen, a league source conveyed on Tuesday. James, who is entering his 24th NBA season, has a history with the Heat. James spent four seasons with the Heat from 2010 to 2014, winning NBA championships with the organization in 2012 and 2013 in four NBA Finals appearances. He also was selected as the NBA’s Most Valuable Player two times while with the Heat.

item.title: Kings, Jonathan Mogbo agree to a two-way deal
item.description: Michael Scotto: The Sacramento Kings and Jonathan Mogbo have agreed to a two-way deal, league sources told @hoopshype. Mogbo was the 31st pick of the 2024 NBA Draft and spent the past two seasons with the Toronto Raptors. Agent Austin Walton of NEXT Sports and Kings officials agreed to the deal.

item.title: Blazers head coach Micah Nori: I think we are going to get the best version of Ja Morant
item.description: For two hours, they dined and talked in a South Carolina steakhouse, and what Portland Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori noticed most about his lunch partner was the sincerity of his words, the seriousness of his facial expressions, and the excitement that was unable to be contained. Ja Morant told his new coach that he couldn’t wait to play for the Blazers. “I think we are going to get the best version of Ja,” Nori said. “I think we are going to get a motivated Ja.”

item.title: “The way he was talking, the way he looked … the …
item.description: When Nori settled into the steakhouse booth on Tuesday, he saw none of the petulance, none of the defiance, none of the attitude that has colored Morant’s image. Nori said he couldn’t help but notice the way Morant talked, and the way he carried himself. There was a seriousness, an enthusiasm, a focus. “The way he was talking, the way he looked … the intent he had, you could just tell in his face that he missed basketball,” Nori said. “And he assured that we were going to get the best Ja and tha

item.title: “He’s excited to be on a team with vets like Dame and …
item.description: “He’s excited to be on a team with vets like Dame and Jrue, and he loves the young talent of Deni (Avdija), Scoot, (Donovan) Clingan, (Toumani) Camara … I mean, he mentioned them all by name,” Nori said. As they left the restaurant, Nori asked Morant what he needed from him. How could he help? “He just said, ‘Make sure I get some Trail Blazers gear as soon as possible so I can start wearing it,’” Nori said.

item.description: That did not immediately mean he was leaving the Lakers. Paul said that several weeks earlier, James still gave his chances of returning to Los Angeles at around 80%. But that number continued to drop as the offseason moved along. Eventually, James reached a firm conclusion. “Once he got to a place to where he said, ‘Listen, man, I understand where things are, and I get it. item.title: “So if it’s about happiness, then it can’t be about …
item.description: Appearing on the latest episode of the “Game Over” podcast with Max Kellerman, Paul explained that James initially seemed likely to return to Los Angeles for another season. But as the offseason unfolded, that confidence faded. “So if it’s about happiness, then it can’t be about money,” Paul said. “If it’s about happiness, because if it’s the most money, then it’s not necessarily the most happiness.”

item.title: With this rule, any foul that would typically result …
item.description: NBA Communications: The one free throw rule will be tested at the upcoming NBA summer leagues. With this rule, any foul that would typically result in one, two or three free throws under standard NBA rules will instead result in a single free throw attempt. That attempt will be worth the same total number of points as the free throws it replaces. Standard NBA free throw rules will apply during the last two minutes of the fourth quarter and throughout overtime.

item.title: The NBA released final accounting on the 2025-26 …
item.description: The NBA released final accounting on the 2025-26 season, revealing basketball-related income was $11.68 billion, up from $10.25 billion the previous year. The BRI means players and owners will roughly split an escrow account of about $580 million set aside to make the math work in the shared-revenue system laid out in the collective bargaining agreement.

item.title: Total salaries and benefits for the 2025-26 season …

Additionally, this was the first season of the NBA’s new 11-year, $76 billion media contracts. Total salaries and benefits for the 2025-26 season were $6.27 billion, above the 51% threshold. The escrow account was divided so 54.8% went to the owners and 45.2% t

item.title: For three straight seasons beginning with 2014-15, …
item.description: The NBA’s escrow system, implemented during the 1999 CBA, has traditionally been set at between 8% and 10% of player compensation. For three straight seasons beginning with 2014-15, 100% of the escrow was returned to players along with a supplemental check as revenues surged and produced an uneven split.

item.title: The Portland resident said he discovered a Los Angeles …
item.description: A thrift store find could now sell for hundreds of thousands of dollars. A routine treasure hunt at a Hillsboro Goodwill store in January has turned into a find of a lifetime for 19-year-old Quinn Brown. The Portland resident said he discovered a Los Angeles Lakers warm-up jacket that has since been authenticated as one worn by NBA legend Wilt Chamberlain.

item.title: For just $3.07, the jacket was his. Brown said he had …
item.description: For just $3.07, the jacket was his. Brown said he had an inkling the jacket may be the real deal. So, he posted a photo of it on Instagram, where it caught the attention of Sotheby’s, one of the world’s largest auction houses. Before long, the jacket was on its way to New York, where it was professionally authenticated through SIA Photo Match.

item.title: The jacket is currently up for auction at Sotheby’s …
item.description: “They said your jacket has been matched to the 1972 NBA Finals. I knew the NBA Finals jersey sold for $4.9 million. That’s the jersey he wore under my jacket,” Brown said. According to Sotheby’s, the jacket was also photo-matched to images of Chamberlain wearing it during the 1972-73 NBA season, his final season in the league. The jacket is currently up for auction at Sotheby’s with an estimated value of $150,000 to $250,000.

item.description: kuz: After sitting here watching NBA free agency this year and overall NBA movement over the past 2 years somebody has to say it.... The new CBA was sold as parity, but the first and second apron are starting to function like a hard cap on player value, team continuity, and player movement. Teams are no longer making purely basketball decisions. They’re making fear-based apron decisions. item.title: Former Kentucky basketball player Kerr Kriisa has been …
item.description: Former Kentucky basketball player Kerr Kriisa has been arrested and indicted on a $2.2 million fraud scheme, the Department of Justice announced on Monday. Kriisa -- a 6-foot-3 guard from Estonia who played at Kentucky, Arizona, West Virginia and Cincinnati over six seasons -- "allegedly carried out a scheme to obtain nearly $2.2 million from multiple victims using false representations, fabricated identities, and deceptive communications," per the DOJ's news release on his arrest.

item.title: Kriisa allegedly ran a four-year scheme that involved …
item.description: According to the Department of Justice, Kriisa allegedly ran a four-year scheme that involved convincing one victim to send him money by saying his mother had cancer and needed treatment. By posing as his mother in another scheme, he allegedly told one victim he needed money to "save" the family's farm. He also allegedly acted as a woman named "Irene" to sign a fraudulent promise to repay one of the victims $100,000 by a February deadline, per the DOJ's indictment.

item.title: Kam Jones questioned his NBA future after he was …
item.description: Pacers rookie Kam Jones questioned his NBA future after he was ordered out of his car at gunpoint following a police chase last year, new body cam footage obtained by The California Post shows. Jones’ dramatic encounter with Indiana State Police occurred in Indianapolis on Oct. 10, 2025, after he allegedly hit speeds of over 100 mph and then refused to immediately pull over.

item.title: “I feel very confused right now,” the basketball …
item.description: Cops were seen in the newly released video training their guns on Jones before they demanded he exit his ride and walk toward them slowly. When Jones, 24, ultimately complied and was placed in handcuffs, he insisted he was not trying to evade them on purpose. “I feel very confused right now,” the basketball player said. “Honestly, I saw your right blinker on, so I’m like, ‘Is he trying to get by me?’ So, I was trying to get out your way.” Jones explained he was driving quickly because he was lat

item.title: “I’m going to jail?” he asked. “Yeah,” one cop …
item.description: “I’m going to jail?” he asked. “Yeah,” one cop responded. “Reckless driving and resisting law enforcement.” “I didn’t know you were trying to pull me over, though,” Jones said. “You could have fooled me,” the officer said. As police took Jones toward the back of a squad car, a Pacers assistant coach appeared on the scene. However, cops would not let the two communicate and the Indiana staffer drove off moments later.

item.title: One officer then asked about Jones’ life, and at one …
item.description: One officer then asked about Jones’ life, and at one point, the cop noticed Jones’ 6-foot-3 frame and wondered if he played point guard or shooting guard. Jones then somberly said, “I’m about to be nothing no more.” “Why not?” the cop asked. “I just didn’t realize I was driving that fast,” Jones said.

item.title: A new state-commissioned report found most comparable …
item.description: A new state-commissioned report found most comparable NBA arena renovation deals included significant private investment or long-term revenue sharing — unlike the proposal currently being negotiated for the Moda Center. The report, required by the legislation authorizing Oregon's $365 million commitment to the project, also highlights disagreement between the state's consultant and the Trail Blazers over which NBA cities should serve as the best comparisons for Portland.

item.title: Four of the cities in the state's analysis received …
item.description: Four of the cities in the state's analysis received private contributions ranging from 18% to 62% of the project. Some cities secured annual rent payments or other revenue sharing to offset public funding. Among the state's six comparable projects, only Memphis, where negotiations are ongoing, and Orlando relied entirely on public funding for construction.

item.title: Western conference executives believe LeBron James will sign with Warriors
item.description: Some executives are skeptical of the growing narrative that a third Cleveland stint is a certainty. Multiple Western Conference executives told Front Office Sports they expect James to sign with the Warriors over the Cavaliers for his 24th NBA season. While Cleveland has been the favorite on prediction markets—and Bill Simmons said the move was a “done deal”—some executives believe Golden State is still a real player for James’s services.

item.title: “I don’t believe he is chasing a ring,” Cooper told …
item.description: After initially holding optimism that LeBron James would return to the Los Angeles Lakers, Michael Cooper hardly wanted to make another prediction on James’ future. "The process was quite long, and we had many conversations, but Lithuania, Zalgiris, and basketball in Lithuania definitely played a big role," Valanciunas said. "The fans and what Zalgiris have been building here over the past few years also really impressed me, so I wanted to be part of it."

item.title: Raptors paused Kawhi Leonard trade when asked to assume risk of any penalties from Clippers contract investigation
item.description: The tipping point to put on hold the trade of Kawhi Leonard to the Raptors came when it was time for Toronto to officially sign off on the conditions of the deal. The way the summer player market has unfolded, the team’s salary cap situation and the kind of free agents still available, there’s no other major deals to make.

I got in the groove that day, and it really kind of set the tone for the rest of my career,” Morrow said. “Like, it really etched me in stone.”

item.title: “Sure, people say, ‘Well, summer league doesn’t mean …

item.title: Lakers owner Mark Walter under federal investigation for potential financial improprieties
item.description: The billionaire Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter’s sprawling investment empire is facing scrutiny from US prosecutors, who have been investigating potential financial improprieties at two of his insurance companies and at Guggenheim Partners LLC, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Prosecutors want to know whether the companies failed …
item.description: The insurers received grand jury subpoenas in February, according to previously unreported regulatory filings. Prosecutors want to know whether the companies failed to disclose that certain private credit investments backed other parts of Walter’s business empire, the companies said in the June 26 filings. That investigation is being conducted in parallel with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, the companies said.

item.title: Walter is best known for his ownership stakes in …
item.description: Walter controls the insurers and has a stake in Guggenheim through his TWG Global holding company. Walter is best known for his ownership stakes in premier sports teams, including Major League Baseball’s Dodgers, the Los Angeles Lakers basketball team and the UK’s Chelsea soccer club.

item.title: Citing that view of the city’s business climate and …
item.description: The official noted that the Trail Blazers ranked last in the NBA in sponsorships last season and were the only team in the league not to secure a jersey patch sponsor, issues that point to economic realities that the ownership group underestimated. Citing that view of the city’s business climate and rising construction costs, the official added, “The deal doesn’t get better. It gets worse with time.”

item.title: NBA champion Kevin Love, towering over everyone at 6 …
item.description: On an overcast Thursday morning at a Lake Oswego storefront hidden away in an alley, NBA champion Kevin Love, towering over everyone at 6 feet, 10 inches, was preparing to open the doors of his new store for the first time. Aptly called The Alley, this new store is a Topps Authorized Direct Partner and sells trading cards, carrying everything from packs of Pokémon cards to a special, mint condition shiny Michael Jordan card that’ll set you back $375.

item.title: The initial lease they signed can be as long as six …
item.description: The Alley is at 435 Second St. in Lake Oswego. The space is 2,100 square feet. The initial lease they signed can be as long as six years. “You’re getting a new series of demographic and generations of collectors, which makes it a fun space,” Kevin said.

item.title: Khris Middleton on returning to Wizards: 'Really excited to see what this team can do'
item.description: Back in Washington, Khris Middleton is eager to guide an intriguing roster brimming with young talent and dynamic additions. "Definitely a talented group," Middleton said of the Wizards. "Young guys have made a huge jump development-wise since they’ve been drafted. Year three for a lot of them... throw in the No. 1 pick, AJ (Dybantsa), also—really excited to see what this team can do."

item.title: "It’s going by fast. Time is coming to an end, but …
item.description: Looking back on a career spanning more than 800 regular-season games and over 13,000 points, Middleton isn't taking a single moment for granted. "It’s going by fast. Time is coming to an end, but each year I’ve been enjoying it. That is what it's about," Middleton reflected. "To be heading to my 15th year, unbelievable— something I’ve been working for a really long time and still working towards."

item.title: "This was my face too when I found out," Middleton …
item.description: The past year has brought plenty of roster shuffling, including a brief detour through Dallas right as his family was settling into the nation's capital. But as Middleton sees it, that’s just the nature of the business. "This was my face too when I found out," Middleton said, laughing as he recalled finding out about the trade just minutes before it went public. "We all found out a couple minutes before it went live."

item.title: A new research paper by 2 Texas Tech professors, James …

The most straightforward path is waiving either Dalen Terry, who is non-guaranteed, or Jabari Walker, who has a $250,000 partial guarantee. item.title: "Growing up in my neighborhood, the cool sports for us …
item.description: Hamilton wishes he had had the opportunity to learn the game as a child, but he was well aware that this was not possible due to the lack of golfing resources in Black and Latino communities. "Growing up in my neighborhood, the cool sports for us were basketball and football. We were never introduced to golf," Hamilton said. "Now, I take pride in showing that golf is cool and fun. It is a great social environment."

item.title: "I'm not like Larry Brown yelling and screaming at all …
item.description: During the event, he spent much of the day teaching the kids the fundamentals of golf, serving as a coach in a way that was quite different from Larry Brown's coaching methods. "I'm not like Larry Brown yelling and screaming at all the kids," Hamilton said. "Golf is a game I am truly passionate about, and I love that Bank of America is breaking down barriers to the sport for kids in our community through Golf with Us."

item.title: Mutual interest between Cavs, Jonathan Kuminga

item.title: “Jonathan likes the Cavs, likes (coach) Kenny …
item.description: “Jonathan likes the Cavs, likes (coach) Kenny Atkinson, and (star) Donovan Mitchell likes him,” Turner, Kuminga’s agent, said in a brief interview. Turner said Kuminga is fond of Cleveland generally and spent two months training there last summer. Kuminga has a relationship with Atkinson from when the coach was an assistant under Steve Kerr at Golden State. While both sides confirmed interest, it is unclear which avenue the Cavs might take to acquire Kuminga if they decide on that path.

item.title: Kansas City mayor makes push to land NBA franchise
item.description: At a media availability Friday, Mayor Quinton Lucas raised the idea of Kansas City getting back into the NBA conversation, whether through franchise relocation or league expansion. “I think we continue to be, probably, the supportive sports city in America,” Lucas said.

item.title: “I think we could easily support an NBA team, and I …
item.description: Lucas pointed to the city’s recent track record as proof. “You saw it with the World Cup, with a lot of people who may not have been soccer fans before. But Kansas City unified, invested,” he said. He said that same energy could translate to the NBA. “I think we could easily support an NBA team, and I think as conversations go on, either for franchises themselves looking for different places or for NBA expansion,” he said.

item.title: Caitlin Clark on LeBron James joining Philadelphia: 'No way! I just pitched him for the Pacers'
item.description: Caitlin Clark had just finished making her own pitch for LeBron James when the actual news broke. The Indiana Fever star was speaking to reporters ahead of WNBA All-Star weekend Friday in Chicago when word came down that James had joined the Philadelphia 76ers – moments after Clark had jokingly lobbied for him to join her own Indiana Pacers. “No way! I just pitched him for the Pacers -- it didn’t get to him fast enough,” Clark said during her media availability. “The 76ers? Wow, wow.”

item.title: “Welcome to the city!” Barkley wrote on social media. …
item.description: Among those caught up in the excitement of James’ decision? Saquon Barkley, the Eagles’ superstar running back who welcomed James to Philadelphia on Friday afternoon. “Welcome to the city!” Barkley wrote on social media. “Let me know when you tryna tee it up.” Barkley is an avid golfer, and James has just recently gotten into it. Surely, they’ll be playing together in the near future.

item.title: “It’s not helpful. It’s not effective. I just want to …

item.title: 18 collegiate players will earn more than LeBron James
item.description: At least 18 men’s college basketball players will earn more than LeBron James next season. The last time that was true? Try the 2002-03 season, when James was a senior at St. Vincent-St. Mary High in Akron, Ohio. Technically, any college hooper on scholarship “made” more than James at the time, though prominent players were getting more than room, board and tuition long before the current era of compensation in the millions.

item.title: AS Monaco have received another extension from the …
item.description: AS Monaco have received another extension from the French Basketball Federation’s Appeals Chamber as the club continues working to complete a takeover led by former NBA All-Star Jamal Mashburn. As BeBasket reports, Monaco now have until Thursday, July 30, at 23:59 to submit all the documents required for admission to the 2026-27 Betclic ELITE season. The DNCCG, French basketball’s financial watchdog, rejected the club’s registration at the first instance.

item.title: Other potential buyers have reportedly withdrawn, …
item.description: Other potential buyers have reportedly withdrawn, leaving Mashburn’s Helen Holdings investment fund as Monaco’s only remaining takeover candidate. According to the court-appointed administrator cited by BeBasket, Monaco’s financial obligations amount to €24 million. That figure includes €8 million in liabilities recorded at the end of June and the €16 million provided by the Principality to enable the club to complete last season.

The Milwaukee Bucks, Atlanta Hawks and Los Angeles Clippers are also interested in acquiring Watson through potential sign-and-trade opportunities, the league sources said.

item.title: Denver is attempting to move a contract or two to get …

The Nuggets’ payroll is in the second apron because they decided to match Oklahoma City’s offer sheet for Jones. Denver is attempting to move a contract or two to get back under the second apron and clear enough money to retain Watson, the league sources said.

When pressed further on possible investment, Hankins said it sounds like public negotiations, which his team is avoiding.

Though he has yet to change the city’s policies, New York mayor Zohran Mamdani campaigned on further restrictions for air travel, saying last April that “we must end non-essential helicopter flights immediately.

They were charging among the lowest prices of the 16 teams in the playoffs. It is a hard place to make money."

item.title: Austin is a robust market that is the economic inverse …

That said, everything is negotiable, and Austin is a robust market that is the economic inverse of Portland. Even though things have slowed slightly in Austin, it has had explosive growth, it has a great sponsorship base, tons of tech money. It would be a huge boon to the NBA.

Where Tom Dundon is not the one who is making this happen, he is simply playing his part and executing a vision that predates him entering the picture."
